735	=================== split-at-shot-changes
736	---
737	title: "Split at Shot Changes"
738	description: "Cut a finished edit, a download or a stream recording into one clip per shot, with the cuts found on your Mac."
739	---
740	
741	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
742	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
743	
744	Split at Shot Changes takes a clip that already has cuts in it, such as a finished edit, a downloaded clip or a stream recording, and cuts it at each one, giving you one clip per shot.
745	
746	<AtAGlance
747	  menu="Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes"
748	  tools={['split_at_shots', 'get_media_analysis']}
749	  needs="Nothing. The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
750	/>
751	
752	## Split a clip at its shot changes
753	
754	<Steps>
755	
756	1. Select one or more clips that show a video file's picture.
757	
758	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. It has no shortcut.
759	
760	3. If Frame Job hasn't looked at this footage yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#while-the-cuts-are-found) to finish.
761	
762	</Steps>
763	
764	Each selected clip is cut at every hard cut inside the part of the file it plays. All the cuts are one undo step, named Split at Shot Changes.
765	
766	The command is greyed out until a selected clip shows a video file's picture. Anything else in the selection is left alone: text, an image, a freeze frame, an audio file, a nest, or a clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
767	
768	If the footage holds no shot change inside any selected clip, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.
769	
770	## While the cuts are found
771	
772	When the footage has already been read, the split lands at once. Otherwise the **Analyzing** sheet appears, with one row per file:
773	
774	| A file's row reads | What it means |
775	| --- | --- |
776	| Waiting | Its first frame hasn't been read yet. |
777	| A percentage, with a bar | How much has been read. |
778	| Done | Its cuts have been found. |
779	
780	The split lands as soon as every file is done. Editing commands are off while the sheet is up.
781	
782	**Stop** closes the sheet and changes nothing. Frame Job saves what it has found every 30 seconds or so, and that stays in the cache, so a long file doesn't start from nothing next time.
783	
784	If the project changes anyway while the sheet is up, for example through an agent, nothing is split, and the inspector says to choose the command again.
785	
786	## What counts as a hard cut
787	
788	A hard cut is a change from one picture to another between two frames. Frame Job compares each frame's colours with those of the frames before it. It's a plain measurement of the picture, with no machine learning, so the same footage always gives the same cuts.
789	
790	- A gradual dissolve isn't a cut.
791	- A single flash frame isn't a cut, because the picture after it matches the one before.
792	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can be found as one cut.
793	- Two shots with very similar colours can be missed, because the comparison looks at colour rather than at what's in the frame.
794	- Of two cuts within 12 frames of each other in the file, only the stronger is found.
795	
796	## Found on this Mac and cached
797	
798	Shot changes are found on your Mac. Nothing is sent anywhere and you don't need a key.
799	
800	The results are kept in the project's cache, so a second split of the same footage starts at once. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).
801	
802	## Where the cuts land
803	
804	Each cut lands on the project's frame grid, worked out through the clip's speed, [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) and [reversal](/speed/reverse/). In a project whose frame rate differs from the file's, that's the nearest project frame.
805	
806	A cut within one frame of either end of a clip isn't made, so you won't get a piece one frame long at a clip's edge.
807	
808	Each cut is an ordinary [split](/editing/splitting/), so actions, word timings and graphics divide the same way.
809	
810	## Locked tracks and linked sound
811	
812	A selected clip on a locked track is still cut. Its linked sound is cut with it when the sound's track is unlocked, as with [Split](/editing/splitting/#linked-sound).
813	
814	## The clip ceiling
815	
816	A project holds up to 4,096 clips, counting the clips inside nests. If the splits would pass that, nothing is split at all, and the inspector says how many clips the command would add and how many more would fit. The count includes each linked clip the splits also cut.
817	
818	## When it can't run
819	
820	Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector:
821	
822	| What happened | What to do |
823	| --- | --- |
824	| A file is missing or can't be read | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), then choose the command again. |
825	| The analysis of a file failed | The message names the file and the reason. Nothing is split. |
826	| The analysis is no longer in the project's cache | Choose the command again, and Frame Job reads the file again. |
827	
828	## With an agent
829	
830	`split_at_shots` works on the clips it's given, and lists any it can't cut under `skipped`. Without a list, it takes every clip of a video file on an unlocked track, so a clip on a locked track is cut only when it's named. It shows no sheet. It waits up to 60 seconds for the cuts, and if they aren't ready it stops without splitting and keeps what it has saved so far, so calling it again carries on.
831	
832	With no cut inside any clip, it reports that no clips were added and leaves no undo step. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split_at_shots).
833	
834	[`get_media_analysis`](/mcp/tools-analysis/#get_media_analysis), with the kind `shots`, reads a file's cuts without splitting anything. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
835

1	=================== delete-clips
2	---
3	title: "Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift"
4	description: "Remove clips or a stretch of the timeline, and choose whether the hole stays open or closes up."
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	There are two delete keys, and the difference between them is what happens to the hole. <kbd>⌫</kbd> leaves it open, so everything else keeps its timing. <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> closes it, so the rest of the timeline moves left.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
13	  keys={['⌫', '⌘⌫']}
14	  where="The Ripple Delete button in the timeline bar"
15	  tools={['delete', 'ripple_delete', 'lift_range', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
16	/>
17	
18	## Choose a delete
19	
20	Each key acts on the selection, or on the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when nothing is selected.
21	
22	| | Clips selected | Nothing selected, a range set |
23	| --- | --- | --- |
24	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Delete** | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** removes what's in the range and moves nothing. |
25	| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips and closes each hole. | **Ripple Delete:** removes what's in the range and closes the hole. |
26	
27	A selection takes priority over a range, so [deselect](/timeline/selecting-clips/) first to act on the range. An empty range is ignored. With nothing to remove, both menu items are greyed out and the keys beep.
28	
29	## Delete clips and leave a gap
30	
31	Select the clips and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. They go, the gaps stay, and nothing else moves. It's one undo step, named Delete.
32	
33	- A picture takes its [linked sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) with it, unless the sound's track is locked.
34	- A linked sound clip goes alone, and leaves its picture silent.
35	- A clip on a locked track that you selected by clicking is still removed.
36	
37	## Ripple delete clips
38	
39	Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, or use the timeline bar's button. The clips go, and each hole closes: everything later on every unlocked track moves left. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.
40	
41	- Each clip's linked partner on an unlocked track goes too, whichever half you selected.
42	- A clip on a locked track that you selected is removed, but clips on locked tracks don't move.
43	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.
44	
45	:::caution
46	Unlike <kbd>⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> ignores a [selected action](/motion/select-an-action/). With an action selected it ripple-deletes the whole clip. Undo brings it back.
47	:::
48	
49	## Lift a range
50	
51	Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, and what lies between is removed. Nothing moves, markers included. It's one undo step, named Lift.
52	
53	Lift is the safe cut when a mix or a caption track is already timed, because everything after the range keeps its moment. Clips on locked tracks are neither cut nor removed. If the range held nothing to remove, Frame Job beeps.
54	
55	## Ripple delete a range
56	
57	Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, what lies between is removed, and the hole closes. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.
58	
59	Clips on locked tracks are neither cut, removed nor moved, even inside the range. Everything else after the range moves left by its length, so a locked track falls out of step with the rest. That's what the lock is for.
60	
61	## How a ripple closes holes
62	
63	Each hole closes with one shift of everything after it, so clips that touched before still touch.
64	
65	- A clip past several holes moves by their combined length. Two removed clips that touch leave one hole.
66	- A clip moves if it starts at or after the end of the hole. When you ripple-delete clips, a clip on another track that spans the hole stays where it is, and isn't shortened.
67	- A clip's linked partner on an unlocked track moves with it.
68	- Markers stay at their times, because a marker inside a removed stretch would have nowhere to go.
69	- A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. A ripple is never stopped by the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
70	
71	One thing does stop a ripple. If it would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline, as a sound leading its picture in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) can, nothing moves, and the foot of the inspector names both clips.
72	
73	## Ripple delete several ranges
74	
75	An agent can cut a list of time ranges out of the timeline as one edit and one undo step, with [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges). It shows as Ripple Delete under **Edit ▸ Undo**. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) make the same cut from their sheets.
76	
77	Ranges that touch or overlap merge into one before anything is cut, so two ranges that meet leave one hole, and all the cuts use times from the timeline as it was before the edit. Each range then behaves as [a ripple-deleted range](#ripple-delete-a-range) does: locked tracks are left alone and markers don't move. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).
78	
79	## When the delete keys do something else
80	
81	<kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the first of these it finds:
82	
83	1. Words or a pause selected in the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/), while that tab has the focus. They ripple out and the gap closes, as deleting text does.
84	2. A [selected action](/motion/change-an-action/). The action goes and its clip stays.
85	3. The selected clips.
86	4. The in/out range.
87	
88	<kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> follows the same order without the second step.
89	
90	While you type in a text field, both menu items are greyed out, so <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> edit the text. That covers the timecode fields, a rename and a text clip.
91	
92	While a point is selected in a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point and **Edit ▸ Delete** is greyed out.
93	
94	## With an agent
95	
96	[`delete`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#delete) and [`ripple_delete`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete) take a list of clips. [`lift_range`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#lift_range) and [`ripple_delete_range`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_range) take a start and an end time, `from` and `to`, and `to` has to be after `from`. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

105	=================== close-gaps
106	---
107	title: "Close gaps and insert time"
108	description: "Close an empty stretch of a track with a double-click or Close Gap, and open room on the timeline when you need it."
109	---
110	
111	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
112	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
113	
114	Closing a gap pulls everything after it back to meet what's before it, on every unlocked track, so the timeline stays in sync. Opening room does the opposite.
115	
116	<AtAGlance
117	  menu="Clip ▸ Close Gap"
118	  where="Double-click an empty stretch of a lane"
119	  tools={['close_gap', 'insert_time']}
120	/>
121	
122	## Double-click a gap
123	
124	Double-click an empty stretch of a track's lane. Everything after the gap, on every unlocked track, moves left by the gap's length. It's one undo step, named Close Gap.
125	
126	This only works on a lane. Above the first lane or below the last there's no track, so there's nothing to close.
127	
128	## Close the gap under the playhead
129	
130	Move the playhead into a gap and choose **Clip ▸ Close Gap**. It has no shortcut.
131	
132	It works on the current track: the selected clip's track or, with nothing selected, the front track. The result is the same as a double-click. The command is available when the timeline has clips.
133	
134	## What moves
135	
136	- A gap is the empty stretch between two clips on that track. A gap before the first clip closes back to the start of the timeline.
137	- Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after the far side of the gap moves left. A clip on another track that spans that point stays where it is.
138	- A moved clip's [linked partner](/audio/detach-and-attach/) moves too, when its track is unlocked.
139	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.
140	- A clip that ends up overlapping the one before it, within the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), gets a Cross Dissolve.
141	
142	## When a gap won't close
143	
144	A gap closes completely or not at all. Frame Job beeps, moves nothing and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector when:
145	
146	| What's wrong | What to do |
147	| --- | --- |
148	| The playhead is on a clip, not in a gap | Move the playhead into the gap, or check the current track. |
149	| No clip follows the gap on that track | There's nothing to pull back. |
150	| The track is locked | [Unlock it](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). Its clips are the ones that would stay behind. |
151	| Closing it would push clips into an overlap the overlap rule forbids, on any track that moves | Trim or move those clips first. |
152	| A linked clip would go before the start of the timeline | Happens when a sound leads its picture, as in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). Trim the front of the sound so it leads by less. |
153	
154	## Insert time
155	
156	Inserting time opens empty room. Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later by a length, and so does every marker at or after that point, unlike a ripple.
157	
158	Clips that span the point stay put, so nothing is cut. To open room inside a clip, [split](/editing/splitting/) it first.
159	
160	Inserting time has no menu item or gesture of its own. An ⌥-drop [insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) and [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) both do it as part of their edit, and an agent can do it directly.
161	
162	## Open room by hand
163	
164	<Steps>
165	
166	1. Move the playhead to where the room should start.
167	
168	2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd> (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**) to select every clip that starts at or after the playhead.
169	
170	3. Drag the selected clips later, or press <kbd>⇧.</kbd> to [nudge](/editing/nudge-clips/) them 10 frames at a time.
171	
172	</Steps>
173	
174	This differs from inserting time in two ways: it also moves the selected clips on locked tracks, and it leaves markers where they are. Start the drag on a clip on an unlocked track, because a clip on a locked track can't be grabbed.
175	
176	## With an agent
177	
178	[`close_gap`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#close_gap) takes a track and a time inside the gap, and stops for the same reasons as the menu item. [`insert_time`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#insert_time) takes the point to open room at and how much room to open. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

186	=================== duplicate-clips
187	---
188	title: Duplicate clips
189	description: Put copies of the selected clips straight after them with one key, or drag copies to exactly where you want them.
190	---
191	
192	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
193	
194	Duplicate makes copies of clips without going through the clipboard. Press a key to put them right after the originals, or hold ⌥ and drag them where you want them.
195	
196	<AtAGlance
197	  menu="Edit ▸ Duplicate"
198	  keys={['⌘D', '⌥-drag']}
199	  where="The Duplicate button in the timeline bar"
200	  tools={['duplicate', 'move_clip']}
201	/>
202	
203	## Duplicate the selection
204	
205	Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. **Edit ▸ Duplicate** and the timeline bar's **Duplicate** button do the same. With nothing selected, the menu item is greyed out and the button beeps.
206	
207	The button sits in the [timeline bar](/getting-started/editor-window/#timeline-bar) with the other one-click clip tools, which split, trim, ripple delete and add markers, text and shapes.
208	
209	Each copy goes on the same track as its original, starting right after the selection's span. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing: if it runs from 10 s to 14 s, every copy starts 4 s later than its original.
210	
211	The copies are one undo step, called Duplicate.
212	
213	## Drag a copy
214	
215	To place copies somewhere else, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press on a clip, then drag. The copies follow the pointer and the originals stay where they are.
216	
217	- If the clip you press is part of the selection, the whole selection is copied. If it isn't, only that clip is.
218	- The copies snap and change tracks as a [move](/editing/move-clips/) does. Drop past the top or bottom of the stack to make a new track for them.
219	- A spot the timeline can't take is skipped. The copies stay at the last spot along the drag that worked, and if none did, nothing changes.
220	- The whole drag is one undo step, called Duplicate Clips.
221	
222	Hold only <kbd>⌥</kbd>. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on a clip is a [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/), not a copy.
223	
224	:::caution
225	An ⌥-drag makes its copies by duplicating first, so it needs the room a <kbd>⌘D</kbd> would need. If Duplicate [wouldn't work](#when-duplicate-wont-work) at that moment, because the next clip is hard up against the selection, the drag moves the originals instead. Undo it, then [copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) the clip, which has no such limit.
226	:::
227	
228	## What a copy keeps
229	
230	A copy is the whole clip: its source, trim, speed, name, label, picture and sound settings, and actions. From then on it's a clip of its own, so changing one doesn't change the other.
231	
232	- **Linked clips.** If a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), its partner is copied too and the two copies are linked to each other. A partner on a locked track isn't copied.
233	- **Nest clips.** A copy of a nest clip made with Duplicate or ⌥-drag shows the same nest as the original, so an edit inside one shows in both. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).
234	
235	## When Duplicate won't work
236	
237	Copies follow the same [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) as any other placement, and Frame Job doesn't push later clips out of the way.
238	
239	- A copy may overlap the clip after it by up to half of the shorter clip. The overlap gets a Cross Dissolve, as any new overlap does. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
240	- A longer overlap stops the duplicate. Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
241	- An adjustment clip can't overlap anything, so a copy of one needs clear space.
242	
243	To duplicate into a tight edit, open room first or use **Edit ▸ Copy** and **Edit ▸ Paste**. A paste that has no room goes on a new track.
244	
245	## With an agent
246	
247	`duplicate` takes the clips to copy and puts the copies straight after them, as <kbd>⌘D</kbd> does. There's no agent version of an ⌥-drag: follow `duplicate` with [`move_clip`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip) to put the copies somewhere else. Both also work inside a nest. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#duplicate).
248

255	=================== copy-and-paste
256	---
257	title: Copy, cut and paste
258	description: Copy clips to the clipboard and paste them at the playhead, in the same project or another one, keeping their arrangement.
259	---
260	
261	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
262	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
263	
264	The clipboard carries clips from one place to another: later in the same timeline, or into a different project. Pasted clips land at the playhead and keep the arrangement you copied.
265	
266	<AtAGlance
267	  menu={['Edit ▸ Copy', 'Edit ▸ Cut', 'Edit ▸ Paste']}
268	  keys={['⌘C', '⌘X', '⌘V']}
269	  tools="paste"
270	/>
271	
272	## Copy and paste clips
273	
274	<Steps>
275	
276	1. Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Copy**. The clipboard holds the clips and a note of the media files they show.
277	
278	2. Move the playhead to where they should go.
279	
280	3. Press <kbd>⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste**.
281	
282	</Steps>
283	
284	The pasted clips are selected, so you can drag or style them straight away. The paste is one undo step, called Paste, and you can paste the same clips as many times as you like.
285	
286	**Copy** and **Cut** are greyed out with nothing selected. **Paste** needs no selection. It's greyed out unless Frame Job clips are on the clipboard, because it never pastes another app's text or files.
287	
288	While you're typing in a field, these keys act on the text in the field, not on clips.
289	
290	## Cut clips
291	
292	Press <kbd>⌘X</kbd> or choose **Edit ▸ Cut**. The clips go on the clipboard and are then deleted, leaving gaps, exactly as <kbd>⌫</kbd> does. To close the gaps as well, see [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).
293	
294	A cut is one undo step, called Cut. If the clips can't be copied, Frame Job beeps and deletes nothing.
295	
296	## Where pasted clips land
297	
298	Paste keeps the arrangement you copied.
299	
300	- **In time.** The earliest clip lands at the playhead, and every other clip keeps its distance from it. Everything lands on a frame.
301	- **Across tracks.** Each clip keeps its place in the stack, counted back from the front. A clip copied from the front track lands on the front track, and one copied from the second track down lands on the second track down. A selection across two lanes pastes back onto two lanes.
302	- **Missing tracks.** If the project has too few tracks, new ones are added at the back.
303	
304	## When there's no room
305	
306	A paste isn't turned down for lack of room. A clip that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) on its track goes on a new track at the front, so it stays visible over what was already there.
307	
308	A smaller overlap is allowed, as it is for any placement: up to half of the shorter clip. The clip stays on its track and the overlap gets a Cross Dissolve. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
309	
310	## Paste into another project
311	
312	Copy in one project, switch to another and paste. The clips stay on the clipboard, so the other project can be opened before or after you copy.
313	
314	- **Media.** Files are matched by their path. A file the project already has is reused, and one it doesn't have is added to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/), with the same checks an import makes. Only files the pasted clips use come across, including the `.cube` file of a [look](/color/luts/) and the LUT of [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
315	- **Frame rate.** Pasted clips are snapped to this project's frame rate.
316	- **New clips.** What lands is a new set of clips, so you can paste them again into the project they came from.
317	
318	A graphic clip brings its name and not its files. In a project without that graphic, the clip draws a red error card until you add a graphic of the same name. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
319	
320	## A detached sound comes along
321	
322	When a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), selecting its picture copies both, so the pair pastes as a linked pair. Selecting the sound on its own copies only the sound, and it pastes as an ordinary clip with no link to any picture.
323	
324	Cut follows the same split. Cutting a picture takes its sound with it, unless the sound is on a locked track. Cutting a detached sound on its own leaves the picture in place, silent.
325	
326	## Copied clips as text
327	
328	Paste into a text editor and you get a one-line summary of what was copied, in the project's timecode:
329	
330	```text
331	Frame Job — 2 clips, 00:00:01:00 to 00:00:04:00
332	```
333	
334	## Good to know
335	
336	:::caution
337	**Nest clips can't be pasted.** The clipboard holds the nest clip but not what's inside it, so **Paste** shows an error and pastes nothing, even if only one of the copied clips is a nest clip. **Cut** still deletes a nest clip, so press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> to bring it back. To make another copy of a nest clip, use [Duplicate or ⌥-drag](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
338	:::
339	
340	- A paste lands whole or not at all. If one clip can't go in, Frame Job shows an error naming it and nothing changes. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), for example, can't be pasted while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open.
341	- Room for a paste isn't unlimited: a project holds up to 64 tracks and 4,096 clips. A paste that would pass either limit shows an error.
342	- Copy and Paste work inside a nest. **Copy** takes the clips you picked and counts their depth against the nest's own tracks, and **Paste** lands in the nest that's open.
343	
344	## With an agent
345	
346	`paste` takes a description of the clips in the same form Copy writes, so an agent can place clips without touching your clipboard. `at` sets the time, the playhead if it's left out, and `track` sets where the front-most copied lane lands, the front track if it's left out. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste).
347	
348	## Related

352	- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)

354	=================== paste-attributes
355	---
356	title: Paste Attributes
357	description: Copy one clip's look and sound settings onto any number of other clips in a single step.
358	---
359	
360	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
361	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
362	
363	Paste Attributes makes other clips look and sound like the one you copied. Set up one clip, then give the same settings to the rest in one undo step.
364	
365	<AtAGlance
366	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
367	  keys="⌥⌘V"
368	  tools="paste_attributes"
369	/>
370	
371	## Paste a clip's attributes
372	
373	<Steps>
374	
375	1. Select the clip that has the settings you want and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
376	
377	2. Select the clips that should take them.
378	
379	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
380	
381	</Steps>
382	
383	The item is available when Frame Job clips are on the clipboard and something is selected. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps. The paste is one undo step, called Paste Attributes.
384	
385	If you copied several clips, only one of them counts: the one that starts earliest. At the same start it's the one on the front-most track.
386	
387	## What travels
388	
389	Settings travel in four groups, and a group is only copied when both clips have it. A movie's settings pasted onto a text clip bring its picture settings and leave the text styling alone, and its sound settings go nowhere.
390	
391	Each group replaces the target's whole group, so it isn't a merge. A shadow on the target disappears if the copied clip had none.
392	
393	| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
394	| --- | --- | --- |
395	| **Video** | Everything about the picture: position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corner radius, blend mode, shadow, reflection, filters, spotlight, obscure regions, chroma key, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, Hide While Silent, motion presets, motion blur, the grade and its look, and the [drawn cursor's](/recording/cursor-settings/) settings | Nothing, apart from an adjustment clip's [qualifier](#adjustment-clips-and-qualifiers) |
396	| **Audio** | Everything about the sound: volume, Mute, fades and their shapes, pan, Mix to mono, channels, Keep pitch, ducking, noise reduction, voice isolation, EQ, hum removal, gate, de-esser, leveller, compressor, limiter and voice effects | Nothing |
397	| **Text** | Font, size, colours, alignment, spacing, case, outline, backdrop, text box width, reveal animation and word caption style | Its own words and their timings |
398	| **Shape** | Fill, stroke, gradient, corner radius and arrowheads | Its kind, its size and the end points of a line |
399	
400	:::caution
401	The Video group includes position and scale. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits.
402	:::
403	
404	A look's `.cube` file comes along too, so a grade pasted from another project keeps its LUT.
405	
406	## What stays on the target
407	
408	Paste Attributes copies how a clip looks and sounds, not what makes it that clip. The target keeps:
409	
410	- its place on the timeline and its length
411	- its speed, including a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/)
412	- its [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/), so nothing animated travels
413	- its transition
414	- its name and label
415	- which halves are [switched on](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/)
416	
417	Graphic properties don't travel either. Use [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/) for those.
418	
419	## Adjustment clips and qualifiers
420	
421	A qualifier belongs to an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), so it follows the kind of clip:
422	
423	| Pasting | The qualifier |
424	| --- | --- |
425	| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
426	| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
427	| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |
428	
429	See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/) for moving a grade between clips.
430	
431	## When a paste stops
432	
433	Some picture settings can't land on some kinds of clip. When one can't, Frame Job shows an error saying why and changes nothing, even on the other selected clips.
434	
435	| The target | Can't take |
436	| --- | --- |
437	| An adjustment clip | Blur, sharpen or pixelate filters, a blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
438	| A nest clip | A blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur, Hide While Silent |
439	| A text, shape or graphic clip | Remove Background |
440	| A movie clip or freeze frame | Remove Background with its subject set to Foreground, which only an image clip can take |
441	| Any clip except a text or adjustment clip | A crop that would leave nothing of it, such as one copied from a much larger source |
442	
443	To get past one, take the setting off the copied clip, copy it again and paste, or select only the clips that can take it.
444	
445	## With an agent
446	
447	`paste_attributes` can do two things the menu item can't.
448	
449	- **Choose the groups.** `groups` names which ones travel, out of `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape` and `graphic`, so `["audio"]` pastes the sound alone and leaves the picture settings. Left out, it behaves as the menu item does, and `graphic` only travels when it's named. An empty list won't run.
450	- **Skip what doesn't fit.** A named group that either side lacks normally stops the paste with an error. With `skip_missing` on, a group the copied clip lacks is dropped and a clip that can't take a group is skipped, so a mixed selection goes through. It's off by default, and only applies with `groups`.
451	
452	See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste_attributes).
453

457	- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
458	- [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/)

460	=================== enable-picture-and-sound
461	---
462	title: Turn a clip's picture or sound off
463	description: What it means when one half of a clip is switched off, which commands do it, and how the clip then looks on the timeline.
464	---
465	
466	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
467	
468	A clip has two halves, its picture and its sound, and each can be switched off while the clip stays where it is. A switched-off half adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and it comes back when the half is switched on again.
469	
470	<AtAGlance
471	  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
472	  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
473	  tools="set_enabled"
474	/>
475	
476	## Turn a half off
477	
478	There's no switch for this in the inspector. Commands flip the halves as part of what they do:
479	
480	| Command | What it switches |
481	| --- | --- |
482	| [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Turns the clip's sound off and adds a sound-only copy on the track below, with its picture off. |
483	| [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Merges a detached pair back into one clip with its sound on. |
484	| [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Can turn off the picture of the camera clips it replaces, and their sound when **Mute the cameras' own sound** is ticked. |
485	
486	To silence a clip's sound by hand, use **Mute** on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To hide its picture, set its [opacity](/canvas/transform/) to 0 or [hide the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
487	
488	## How the clip looks
489	
490	| Switched off | On the timeline |
491	| --- | --- |
492	| The picture of a movie clip | It reads as an audio clip, with the audio tint and symbol, and has no filmstrip. |
493	| The sound | It has no waveform. |
494	| Both | It's dimmed, like a clip on a hidden track. |
495	
496	A clip with its sound off has no **Sound** tab in the inspector, because there's nothing there to adjust. Its **Picture** tab stays, even with the picture off.
497	
498	## Good to know
499	
500	- A clip with its sound off can't be transcribed, and **Remove Silences** doesn't count it as audible.
501	- Copies keep the switches of the clip they came from.
502	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) leaves the target's switches alone.
503	
504	## With an agent
505	
506	`set_enabled` switches either half of any clip directly, which no command in the app does on its own. Give it `video`, `audio` or both, as true or false, and a half you leave out stays as it is. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#set_enabled).
507

513	=================== nests
514	---
515	title: Nests
516	description: Collapse several clips into one clip that moves, trims, fades and transforms as a group, and open it back out when you're done.
517	---
518	
519	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
520	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
521	
522	A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing, and the clips inside stay as you built them.
523	
524	<AtAGlance
525	  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
526	  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
527	  tools={['nest', 'unnest', 'set_clip']}
528	/>
529	
530	## Make a nest
531	
532	<Steps>
533	
534	1. Select the clips.
535	
536	2. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.
537	
538	</Steps>
539	
540	The clips are replaced by one nest clip, which is selected so you can move or transform it straight away. The nest is one undo step, called Nest.
541	
542	The nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end, including any gaps. A matte track is the exception: the nest clip goes on the front-most track that isn't a matte, and a matte only stays one inside the nest if the track it cuts goes in with it. See [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/).
543	
544	A clip's [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) goes in with it, unless the sound is on a locked track.
545	
546	To work on the contents later, double-click the nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/).
547	
548	## What a nest keeps
549	
550	Inside the nest, clips keep their properties, [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) and transitions, their timing relative to each other and their stacking order. The earliest clip starts at 0 on the nest's own timeline.
551	
552	The tracks inside are new, and each keeps the name, the hidden, muted, locked and solo states, and the volume and pan of the track it came from. There are two exceptions:
553	
554	- The track the nest clip lands on still applies its volume and pan over the whole nest clip, so its copy inside starts at full volume and centred. A selection from one track sounds the same nested.
555	- A track [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) isn't copied inside. The one on the nest clip's own track goes on working over the nest clip.
556	
557	The nest clip itself starts at the default position and scale, at full opacity. It has a **Sound** tab only when something inside can make a sound.
558	
559	## Name a nest
560	
561	Nests are named `Nest 1`, `Nest 2` and so on. To give a nest clip your own name, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**), or use the name field at the top of the Clip tab.
562	
563	A double-click on a nest clip opens it, so it doesn't start a rename as it does on other clips.
564	
565	## A nest's size is fixed
566	
567	A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. Changing the [project's size](/projects/canvas-size/) later doesn't re-lay out what's inside, and opening the nest lets you edit its contents but not its size.
568	
569	To change a nest's size:
570	
571	<Steps>
572	
573	1. Press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it.
574	
575	2. Change the project size if you need to.
576	
577	3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd> to nest it again.
578	
579	</Steps>
580	
581	## Un-nest
582	
583	Select one or more nest clips and press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Un-nest**. The item is available when the selection includes a nest clip, and anything else selected is left alone.
584	
585	Every selected nest clip opens back out in one undo step, called Un-nest, or Un-nest Clips for several. What came out is selected.
586	
587	- Clips return at the nest clip's start plus their own times, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's track. Missing tracks are added behind it.
588	- A clip that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) goes on a new front track and isn't lost.
589	- A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents still gives everything back, because trimming a nest hides content and doesn't cut it.
590	- If other clips show the same nest, they keep it. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).
591	
592	:::caution
593	Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume. To change the contents and keep those, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it.
594	:::
595	
596	The settings of the tracks inside the nest don't come out either. Clips that return take on the settings of the timeline tracks they land on.
597	
598	## Nests inside nests
599	
600	A nest can hold other nests, up to eight levels deep. Select a nest clip with other clips and press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or press it while a nest is open.
601	
602	The depth counts the whole project, even while you edit inside a nest, so an edit that looks fine there can still stop at the limit. The same goes for the project's limits of 64 tracks and 4,096 clips, and a nest's own tracks count towards the 64.
603	
604	## When Nest won't work
605	
606	**Clip ▸ Nest** is greyed out with nothing selected, and when the only selected clip is already a nest clip, since wrapping one nest in another on its own changes nothing you can see.
607	
608	With the item available, two things can still stop a nest. Frame Job beeps, changes nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.
609	
610	- **Something unselected is in the way.** The nest clip would overlap a clip you didn't select on its track, by more than the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) allows. This often means an unselected clip sits inside the span. Select it too, or move it.
611	- **The selection holds an adjustment clip.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest.
612	
613	If the nest clip overlaps the clip before it by an amount the rule allows, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
614	
615	## With an agent
616	
617	`nest` can name the nest as it's made, [`set_clip`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_clip) renames a nest clip, and [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/) lists every nest with its own tracks and clips. [`unnest`](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#unnest) opens one nest clip at a time, and gives an error on any other kind of clip. The clips it brings back are new clips, with new ids. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#nest) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
618

641	## Open a nest
642	
643	Double-click a nest clip. You can also select one nest clip and choose **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>).
644	
645	**Clip ▸ Open Nest** needs exactly one nest clip selected, so it's greyed out with two selected. A double-click works whatever else is selected, because it opens the clip you clicked.
646	
647	A nest can hold nests. Open one the same way from inside, down to eight levels.
648	
649	Because a double-click opens a nest clip, it can't rename one. Use **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) or the name field in the Clip tab.
650	
651	## Come back out
652	
653	Choose **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>), or click the [breadcrumb](#use-the-breadcrumb). Either one goes out one level, and the nest clip you went in through is selected again.
654	
655	**Clip ▸ Close Nest** is greyed out at the top level. **Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are both greyed out while you're typing in a field, so <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> stay with the text.
656	
657	## Use the breadcrumb
658	
659	While a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as `Timeline › Intro`, with a back arrow in front of it.
660	
661	- It shows the last two levels: the one you'd return to, then the one you're in, in bold. Hover over it for the full path.
662	- A level is named after the nest clip you went in through, so renaming that clip changes the path.
663	- A long name is shortened in the middle, so `Lower Third 1` and `Lower Third 2` still look different.
664	
665	Click anywhere in the corner to go out one level, the same as <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. A double-click counts as one click, so to go up two levels, click twice with a pause or press <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> twice.
666	
667	With no nest open, the corner is empty and does nothing.
668	
669	## What you see inside
670	
671	The timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips, with time counted from the start of the nest. That's all of its contents, including anything the nest clip's [trim](/editing/nest-copies/#trim-a-nest-clip) is hiding on the outer timeline.
672	
673	The canvas shows the nest at its fixed size, without the nest clip's position, scale, opacity or fades, and you hear it without the nest clip's volume. You're seeing the group by itself, and the nest clip's settings apply again when you leave.
674	
675	## Where the playhead goes
676	
677	The playhead moves with you, so the frame under it doesn't change. It also carries back out. If a nest clip starts at 10 s and the playhead is at 12 s, you go in at 2 s. Move to 3 s, come out, and you're at 13 s.
678	
679	That holds while the playhead is over the nest clip. If it's before the clip when you double-click, you go in at the nest's first frame and come out at the clip's start. If it's past the clip's end, or you move past that point inside, the playhead is on a part of the nest the clip doesn't play, so the canvas inside shows a frame the outer timeline never will.
680	
681	Going in or out also stops playback.
682	
683	## Going in and out isn't an edit
684	
685	Opening or closing a nest makes no undo step and doesn't mark the project as changed.
686	
687	- **Selection:** going in clears the selection. Coming out selects the nest clip again.
688	- **In/out range:** it's cleared both ways, because a range means one thing inside a nest and another on the timeline. You can set a new [range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside, and looping and Ripple Delete use it as they do on the timeline.
689	- **Reopening:** a project always opens on its timeline, even if you saved with a nest open.
690	
691	## Edit inside a nest
692	
693	Every clip edit works inside a nest, with times counted from the start of the nest. That includes **Clip ▸ Nest**, which makes a nest inside this one, and **Clip ▸ Un-nest**.
694	
695	Each edit is one step on the project's single undo history:
696	
697	- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> after you've come out still undoes an edit you made inside.
698	- If an undo removes the nest you're in, you land in the deepest level that's left, and the in/out range clears.
699	
700	When more than one clip shows this nest, your edit reaches all of them. See [Shared copies](/editing/nest-copies/#shared-copies).
701	
702	The nest clip on the outer timeline keeps its length whatever you do inside. Material you add past its end stays hidden until you drag the clip's end out, and if the contents get shorter, the clip shows nothing over what's left of it.
703	
704	## What stays project-wide
705	
706	Some things belong to the project, not to the nest you have open. They still work, and they change the whole project.
707	
708	- **Media:** the Media tab lists the project's media. Adding, relinking or removing a file works as usual. Drag a row from the Media tab onto the nest's timeline to put its clip in the nest. A file dragged from the Finder onto the timeline opens as a project of its own, so add it on the Media tab first.
709	- **The Document tab:** it shows the project's settings. Changing the project's size doesn't change the nest's size, which is [fixed](/editing/nests/#a-nests-size-is-fixed).
710	- **Markers:** the Document tab's list stays, but the ruler shows none. You can still rename a marker, change its **Chapter** box or delete it. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
711	- **Export:** **File ▸ Export…** writes the whole timeline, not the nest. A range you set inside a nest can't be used, so the **Range** pop-up stays on **Whole project**. Close the nest and set the range on the timeline.
712	
713	**File ▸ Save Frame…** is the exception: it saves what the canvas shows, so with a nest open you get a frame of the nest.
714	
715	## What you can't use inside a nest
716	
717	| Command | While a nest is open |
718	| --- | --- |
719	| **Mark ▸ Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker** | Greyed out, and <kbd>M</kbd> beeps. **Go** in the Document tab's Markers list is greyed out too. A marker's time is on the outer timeline, and the playhead inside a nest counts from the nest's start. |
720	| **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** | Greyed out. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) only works on the timeline, never inside a nest. |
721	| **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject** | Greyed out, and the Picture tab has no **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/). |
722	| **File ▸ New Project from Range…** | Greyed out. See [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/). |
723	| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | Greyed out. See [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/). |
724	| **File ▸ Rename Graphic…** | Greyed out. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/). |
725	| **Track ▸ Mix…** | **Compressor** and **Limit peaks** are greyed out, because a nest's mix plays through the track that holds the nest clip. The track's volume and pan still work. |
726	
727	## Limits count the whole project
728	
729	A project holds up to 4,096 clips and 64 tracks, and nests go eight levels deep. Clips and tracks are counted across the timeline and every nest together, and the depth is counted from the timeline. So an edit that looks fine inside a nest can still take the whole project over. When it would, Frame Job shows an alert naming the limit and changes nothing.
730	
731	A nest's contents count once, however many clips show it. Un-nest the last clip showing a nest to take its tracks out of the count. Deleting that clip instead leaves the nest's clips and tracks counted.
732	
733	## With an agent
734	
735	An agent can open a nest in the window with [`set_scope`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_scope), as you would. This only changes the view, so it adds no undo step, and `set_scope` with no arguments comes back out. Given a nest two clips show, it goes in through the earlier one.
736	
737	An agent can also edit inside any nest without opening it, by naming the nest on the edit. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/), which lists the edits that can't be made that way.
738

747	---
748	title: "Shared and independent nest copies"
749	description: "Know which copies of a nest clip edit together, make a copy of your own, and see what trimming a nest clip really does."
750	---
751	
752	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
753	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
754	
755	A nest clip is a view of a [nest](/editing/nests/), not the nest itself. Two clips can show one nest, so an edit inside it reaches both. This page covers which copies share their contents, how to get one that doesn't, and what a trim does to a nest clip.
756	
757	<AtAGlance
758	  menu={['Edit ▸ Duplicate', 'Clip ▸ Split', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest', 'Clip ▸ Nest']}
759	  keys={['⌘D', '⌘T', '⇧⌘G', '⌘G']}
760	  where="⌥-drag a nest clip"
761	  tools={['duplicate', 'split', 'paste', 'unnest', 'nest']}
762	/>
763	
764	## Shared copies
765	
766	These all leave you with clips that show one nest:
767	
768	| Do this | You get |
769	| --- | --- |
770	| **Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>) | A second clip showing the same nest, straight after the selection. |
771	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag a nest clip | A second clip showing the same nest, where you drop it. |
772	| **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>) | Two clips showing the same nest, cut at the playhead. |
773	
774	[Open](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest) any of them and edit, and every clip showing that nest changes.
775	
776	Only the contents are shared. Each nest clip keeps its own place on the timeline, its own length, and its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume.
777	
778	[Un-nesting](/editing/nests/#un-nest) one clip gives you its contents as ordinary clips and leaves the others showing the nest. The nest goes when you un-nest the last clip that shows it.
779	
780	:::caution[A split nest clip starts again]
781	A nest clip always plays from the nest's first frame. So when you split one, the second part starts from the top of the nest, not from where you cut, and the join shows. The same goes for anything else that cuts through a nest clip, such as a ripple delete over a range.
782	
783	To cut the contents at a moment, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and split inside it.
784	:::
785	
786	## Make an independent copy
787	
788	To get a copy you can edit on its own, turn a duplicate back into clips and nest them again.
789	
790	<Steps>
791	
792	1. Select the nest clip and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. The selection stays on the original.
793	
794	2. Click the new copy, then press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it. Its contents come out as ordinary clips, all selected.
795	
796	3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>. Those clips become a new nest of their own.
797	
798	</Steps>
799	
800	Un-nesting drops the copy's own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, so set those again on the new nest clip. The new nest also takes the project's current size, which may differ from the original's. Un-nesting gives back everything in the nest, so a [trim](#trim-a-nest-clip) on the copy is gone too.
801	
802	This separates one level. A nest clip among the contents still shows the same inner nest as the original, so an edit inside that inner nest reaches both. Un-nest it too, before step 3, if you need it separate.
803	
804	:::caution[Copy and Paste don't work on a nest clip]
805	**Edit ▸ Copy** puts the nest clip on the clipboard but not what's inside it. **Edit ▸ Paste** then pastes nothing and shows an alert saying the pasted clip shows a nest "which the payload does not carry". That's true of any selection with a nest clip in it, in this project or another one.
806	
807	**Edit ▸ Cut** still removes the clip, so after a failed paste, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> until it's back.
808	:::
809	
810	## Trim a nest clip
811	
812	Trimming a nest clip changes how much of the nest plays. It never cuts anything out of the nest. The clip always plays from the nest's first frame for as long as the clip lasts, which makes its two edges behave differently from a media clip's:
813	
814	| Drag | What happens |
815	| --- | --- |
816	| The end edge in | The tail of the nest is hidden. |
817	| The end edge out | More of the nest plays. Past the end of the contents, the clip shows nothing. The contents set no limit on how far you can drag. |
818	| The start edge later | The clip starts later and the whole nest moves later with it. The opening still plays, and the tail is what gets hidden. |
819	| The start edge earlier | The nest moves earlier with it, and more of the tail plays. |
820	
821	So you can't hide a nest's opening with a trim. To do that, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it, which changes every clip showing the nest.
822	
823	**Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>) gives back everything, however short the clip was trimmed. Hidden clips come back where they sit in the nest, counted from the nest clip's start, even past the clip's end. One that would then collide with what's after it goes on a new track in front.
824	
825	## With an agent
826	
827	An agent can make the independent copy in one step. `paste` makes a separate nest when it's given the nest's contents as well as the clip, with every level inside it, and editing the copy leaves the original alone. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste).

21	=================== how-edits-work
22	---
23	title: "How edits work"
24	description: What an edit acts on, why clips never push each other, and the rules every timeline edit keeps.
25	---
26	
27	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
28	
29	Every edit in Frame Job acts on something you've already pointed at, and every edit keeps the same few rules. Once you know them, you can tell what a command will touch and why one sometimes won't go through.
30	
31	<AtAGlance
32	  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
33	  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
34	  where="The timeline: the selection, the playhead and the range"
35	  tools={['set_selection', 'set_playhead', 'set_range']}
36	/>
37	
38	## What an edit acts on
39	
40	Most commands act on the selected clips. Some also use the playhead, the in and out range or the current track.
41	
42	| What | What it is | What uses it |
43	| --- | --- | --- |
44	| **The selection** | The clips outlined in coral on the timeline. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/). | Most commands |
45	| **The playhead** | The moment you're looking at. | Split, trim to the playhead, Freeze Frame, Paste, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead |
46	| **The in and out range** | The stretch between the points set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>. <kbd>⌥X</kbd> clears both. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/). | With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range |
47	| **The current track** | The track of the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, it's a track inside the nest. | Close Gap, Select All on Track, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead |
48	
49	A selected clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), shows a dashed ring. Most edits take it along, as long as its track isn't locked.
50	
51	## Clips never push each other
52	
53	A clip you drag never shoves its neighbours out of the way. A place that would need a neighbour to move isn't available, so the clip [stops short of it](/editing/move-clips/#when-a-drop-wont-go-where-you-let-go).
54	
55	Only the edits that are there to move other clips do so: [Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/), [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/), [Insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#insert-a-file), [inserting time](/editing/close-gaps/#insert-time), [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) and [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/). They open or close time across every unlocked track. A [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) stays where it is.
56	
57	## The overlap rule
58	
59	Two clips on one track may overlap a little, and that overlap is a [transition](/motion/transitions/). The rule has three parts:
60	
61	- A clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side.
62	- Each overlap can be at most half the length of the shorter clip.
63	- An adjustment clip can't overlap another clip at all, because it can't take a transition. Fade it with opacity instead.
64	
65	An edit that leaves a clip overlapping the clip before it gives that clip a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition.
66	
67	Moves, trims, nudges, duplicates, gap closes and nests won't break the rule. Paste and Un-nest put a clip that would break it on a new track at the front instead. The rule never stops a ripple delete: a clip it slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.
68	
69	## Times land on frames
70	
71	Every time you give an edit, by dragging or typing, lands on a whole frame of the project's [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/). A moved or trimmed clip goes to the nearest frame, so you can't place a clip between two frames. A time before the start of the timeline stops at 0.
72	
73	The exceptions are the short audio times typed in the **Sound** sub-tab, such as a fade length or a compressor's attack, which keep the value you typed. A fade dragged by its handle on the clip still lands on a frame.
74	
75	A move or a ripple shifts every clip by exactly the same amount, so clips stay in step. At a frame rate that doesn't divide evenly, such as 7 fps, a shifted start can sit off the frame grid by a sliver too small to see.
76	
77	## One frame minimum
78	
79	[Trims](/editing/trimming/) and [rolls](/editing/slip-and-roll/) always leave a clip at least one frame long. The drag stops there, however far you pull.
80	
81	## Project limits
82	
83	| A project holds up to | |
84	| --- | --- |
85	| Clips | 4,096 |
86	| Tracks | 64 |
87	| Levels of nesting | 8 |
88	| Markers | 1,024 |
89	| Media files | 1,024 |
90	
91	Clips and tracks inside nests count towards the same totals as the ones on the timeline. An edit that would pass a limit doesn't happen, and the project stays as it was. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).
92	
93	## When an edit doesn't go through
94	
95	Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and adds no undo step. When a rule stopped the edit, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. An edit that would change nothing beeps too, with no reason given. An edit Frame Job can't carry out at all, such as placing a file shorter than one frame or passing a project limit, shows an alert instead of a beep.
96	
97	A drag is quieter. It stays at the last position the project allows, with no beep. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
98	
99	## With an agent
100	
101	[`set_selection`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_selection), [`set_playhead`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_playhead) and [`set_range`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_range) set the selection, the playhead and the range. They aren't edits and they add no undo step. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
102	
103	An agent's times land on frames too. A negative position on the timeline becomes 0, but a negative length is an error and nothing changes.

113	---
114	title: "Add clips to the timeline"
115	description: Drag a file from the Media tab onto a track or the canvas, and see where it lands and what stops a drop.
116	---
117	
118	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
119	
120	Importing a file puts it in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/), not on the timeline. To use it, drag its row onto a track or onto the preview canvas.
121	
122	<AtAGlance
123	  where={['Media tab ▸ drag a row onto a track', 'Media tab ▸ drag a row onto the preview canvas']}
124	  tools={['add_clip', 'add_track']}
125	/>
126	
127	This page covers files. [Text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) have their own ways in.
128	
129	## Drag media onto a track
130	
131	Drag a row from the Media tab onto a track. The whole file lands as one clip at the pointer, on the nearest frame, and nothing else moves. The drop doesn't snap to the edges of other clips.
132	
133	Hold a modifier as you let go to make room for the file or replace what's there. See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#drop-with-a-modifier).
134	
135	A drop that overlaps a neighbour a little still lands, as long as it keeps to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule), and makes a Cross Dissolve over the overlap.
136	
137	**Edit ▸ Undo** names this step Add Clip.
138	
139	## Drop media on the canvas
140	
141	Drop a row on the preview canvas to add the file at the playhead, on a new track at the front. Use this to lay a file over everything else without looking for a free stretch of track.
142	
143	The new track and the clip are one undo step, Add Clip. Modifier keys do nothing here.
144	
145	## What a new clip covers
146	
147	A new clip starts at the head of the file and runs its whole length, at normal speed. The length rounds down to whole frames, so the clip never runs past the end of the file. That can leave a part of a frame at the tail unused.
148	
149	- **A picture** is 5 seconds long. [Trim it](/editing/trimming/) to any length.
150	- **A file larger than the canvas** is scaled to fit, while **Fit new clips to canvas** is on in the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). It's on by default. A smaller file keeps its size.
151	- **A video or sound file shorter than one frame** of the project can't be placed, and Frame Job says so.
152	
153	## When a drop doesn't land
154	
155	| What happened | What you see |
156	| --- | --- |
157	| The clip would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) | Frame Job beeps, adds nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> to insert or <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> to overwrite as you drop instead. |
158	| You let go above or below the lanes | The drag springs back. Only a [clip already on the timeline](/editing/move-clips/#move-a-clip-to-a-new-track) makes a new track that way. |
159	| You let go in another project's window | The drag springs back. A row can only be placed in its own project. |
160	
161	A `.cube` LUT row doesn't drag at all. [Apply it as a look](/color/luts/) instead.
162	
163	## Good to know
164	
165	- A plain drop onto a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) still places the clip, because nothing has to move.
166	- If the project already has 64 tracks, a drop on the canvas adds the file to the front track instead, and the overlap rule can stop it there.
167	- Files dragged from the Finder are different. On the Media tab they [import](/projects/import-media/). Anywhere else in the window, each opens as a project of its own.
168	
169	## With an agent
170	
171	[`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_clip) places a file on a track at a time you give it, as a plain drop does, and the same rules stop it. To lay a file over everything else, as a drop on the canvas does, an agent calls [`add_track`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#add_track) first. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).

192	  keys={['⌥-drop', '⇧⌥-drop']}
193	  where="Right-click a row in the Media tab"
194	  tools={['insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip']}
195	/>
196	
197	## Place a file at the playhead
198	
199	<Steps>
200	
201	1. Click the file's row in the Media tab.
202	
203	2. Move the playhead to where the file should start.
204	
205	3. To choose the track, select a clip on it. With nothing selected, the file goes on the front track.
206	
207	4. Choose **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** or **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**.
208	
209	</Steps>
210	
211	Neither item has a shortcut. You can also right-click a row and choose either item there, which acts on that row and selects it.
212	
213	The file lands on the [current track](/editing/how-edits-work/#what-an-edit-acts-on). With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, that's a track inside the nest.
214	
215	## Drop with a modifier
216	
217	Drag a row from the Media tab onto a track, and hold a modifier as you let go. Only the keys held at that moment count.
218	
219	| Hold | What the drop does |
220	| --- | --- |
221	| Nothing, or <kbd>⇧</kbd> alone | [Adds the clip](/editing/add-clips/#drag-media-onto-a-track) without moving anything |
222	| <kbd>⌥</kbd> | Inserts at the drop point |
223	| <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> | Overwrites at the drop point |
224	
225	The modifiers only work on a track. A drop on the preview canvas always [adds the file on a new track](/editing/add-clips/#drop-media-on-the-canvas).
226	
227	## Insert a file
228	
229	Insert keeps everything you've already cut, and the timeline gets longer by the length of the file.
230	
231	- If the point falls inside a clip on the destination track, that clip is split there.
232	- Every unlocked track opens up by the file's length. Clips that start at or after the point move later, and so do markers.
233	- The file lands in the room this makes.
234	
235	Only the destination track is cut. A clip on another track that spans the point stays whole and where it is, so a music bed plays on unbroken under the new file. The exception is a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) linked to the clip that was cut. It's cut at the same point, so the pair stays in step.
236	
237	The whole edit is one undo step, Insert.
238	
239	## Overwrite with a file
240	
241	Overwrite moves nothing, and what was there is gone. The timeline only gets longer if the file runs past its end.
242	
243	- The destination track is cut at both ends of the file's length.
244	- Whatever lies between the cuts is removed.
245	- The file lands in the space.
246	
247	Nothing shifts and no other track is touched. The exception is again a detached sound linked to a clip that was cut. It's cut at the same points, and its piece under the new file stays, no longer linked.
248	
249	The whole edit is one undo step, Overwrite.
250	
251	## Good to know
252	
253	- **Locked tracks.** Insert won't work on a locked destination track, because the track can't open up, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Insert elsewhere leaves locked tracks where they are, so their clips can fall out of step with the rest. Overwrite still clears a locked track, because you chose that track and nothing has to move.
254	- **When the menu items are dimmed.** They need a selected row in the Media tab, and that row can't be a `.cube` LUT. A LUT is [applied as a look](/color/luts/), so its right-click **Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** are dimmed too. A filter that hides the selected row clears the selection.
255	- **The length is the whole file.** Both edits place the file from its first frame to its last. To use part of it, [trim the clip](/editing/trimming/) afterwards. After an Insert, trimming leaves a gap, which [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) removes.
256	
257	## With an agent
258	
259	[`insert_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#insert_clip) and [`overwrite_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#overwrite_clip) make the same edits. Each takes a track, a file and a time, so an agent doesn't need the playhead or a selected row, and it can place a file inside a nest without opening it. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
260

267	=================== move-clips
268	---
269	title: "Move clips"
270	description: Drag clips along the timeline and between tracks, alone or together, and see what stops a drop.
271	---
272	
273	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
274	
275	Drag a clip to change when it plays or which track it sits on. The clip you see moving while you drag is the real edit, not a stand-in.
276	
277	<AtAGlance
278	  where="Timeline ▸ drag a clip's body"
279	  tools="move_clip"
280	/>
281	
282	## Drag a clip
283	
284	Drag a clip's body left or right to move it in time, and up or down to move it to another track. A clip stops at the start of the timeline.
285	
286	The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) to nearby edits when snapping is on. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to turn snapping off for that moment.
287	
288	You can't start a drag on a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
289	
290	To drag a copy and leave the original, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press. See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
291	
292	## Move several clips together
293	
294	Select the clips, then drag any one of them. They all move, and they stay the same time and the same number of tracks apart. If the earliest clip reaches the start of the timeline, it stops at 0 and the others keep their distance from it.
295	
296	## Move a clip to a new track
297	
298	Let go above the top lane to make a new track at the front, or below the bottom lane to make a new track at the back. The new track and the move are one undo step.
299	
300	## Clips that come along
301	
302	A clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), moves in time by the same amount and keeps its own track. So you can drag a sound onto a track of its own and its picture stays on its track. A partner on a locked track doesn't move.
303	
304	## Overlaps make a transition
305	
306	If you drop a clip so that it overlaps the clip before it on the track, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. The overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).
307	
308	## When a drop won't go where you let go
309	
310	While you drag, the clip only goes where the project allows. Over a position that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule), it waits at the last position that was allowed, and catches up when you reach one that is.
311	
312	If you let go over a position that isn't allowed, the clip stays at that last allowed position, and a ghost of it slides there from where you let go. If it never reached an allowed position, it's back where it started and nothing has changed. There's no beep and no message.
313	
314	## One undo step per drag
315	
316	A whole drag is one undo step, however long it lasts. **Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) names it Move Clips. A click that doesn't move the clip adds no undo step.
317	
318	## Good to know
319	
320	- A locked clip that's part of a selection moves with the others if you start the drag on an unlocked clip.
321	- Clips selected on more than one track can't make a new track at the front. Let go above the top lane and they stay at the last allowed position. Below the bottom lane works.
322	- With 64 tracks in the project, there's no new track to make. A drop above or below the lanes moves the clips in time only.
323	- To shift clips by an exact number of frames, [nudge them](/editing/nudge-clips/).
324	
325	## With an agent
326	
327	`move_clip` takes the clips and how far to shift them, where a negative shift moves them earlier. Give it a track to move them there as well, and leave that out to keep them on their tracks. Like a drag, it won't break the overlap rule. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip).
328

335	=================== nudge-clips
336	---
337	title: "Nudge clips"
338	description: Move the selected clips one or ten frames at a time from the keyboard.
339	---
340	
341	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
342	
343	A nudge moves the selected clips by an exact number of frames, for the small corrections that are hard to make with a drag.
344	
345	<AtAGlance keys={[',', '.', '⇧,', '⇧.']} tools="move_clip" />
346	
347	## Nudge the selection
348	
349	| Keys | Moves the selection |
350	| --- | --- |
351	| <kbd>,</kbd> | One frame earlier |
352	| <kbd>.</kbd> | One frame later |
353	| <kbd>⇧,</kbd> | Ten frames earlier |
354	| <kbd>⇧.</kbd> | Ten frames later |
355	
356	On a US keyboard, <kbd>⇧,</kbd> and <kbd>⇧.</kbd> are the keys that type `<` and `>`.
357	
358	Each press is one undo step, Nudge Clips. These keys have no <kbd>⌘</kbd>, so while a text field has the focus they type into it instead. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).
359	
360	## Good to know
361	
362	A nudge is an ordinary [move](/editing/move-clips/), with the same rules:
363	
364	- It beeps with nothing selected.
365	- A nudge that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) beeps and changes nothing, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. A nudge that lands on a small enough overlap makes a Cross Dissolve.
366	- The earliest clip stops at the start of the timeline, so <kbd>⇧,</kbd> on a clip three frames from the start moves it three frames. A clip already at the start beeps.
367	- A linked partner on an unlocked track moves with its clip.
368	
369	Unlike a drag, a nudge moves a selected clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). It doesn't snap, and it never changes a clip's track.
370	
371	## With an agent
372	
373	An agent nudges with `move_clip`, giving the shift as a time. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip).
374
