380	=================== trimming
381	---
382	title: "Trim clips"
383	description: Shorten or lengthen a clip by dragging an edge, trimming to the playhead or typing a time.
384	---
385	
386	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
387	
388	Trimming changes where a clip starts or ends without moving the footage inside it. Use it to take the slack off a shot, or to pull back in what you cut too tightly.
389	
390	<AtAGlance
391	  menu={['Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead', 'Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead']}
392	  keys={['W', 'E']}
393	  where={[
394	    'Timeline ▸ drag a clip edge',
395	    'The Trim Start to Playhead and Trim End to Playhead buttons in the timeline bar',
396	    'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing ▸ In and Out',
397	  ]}
398	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
399	/>
400	
401	## Drag an edge
402	
403	Drag either edge of a clip. The edge is the outer 7 points of the clip. The pointer becomes a left-right resize cursor there, and a selected clip shows trim grips.
404	
405	- **A clip 21 points wide or less** on screen is all body, so [zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) to trim it.
406	- **Clips on locked tracks** have no edges to grab and show no resize cursor. <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd> and the **In** and **Out** fields still trim one, if you've selected it by clicking.
407	- **A fade handle or an action band** under the pointer takes the press before the edge does.
408	
409	The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) when snapping is on, and holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> turns snapping off for that moment. The whole drag is one undo step, Trim Clip.
410	
411	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press a media clip's end edge to [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) it instead, which changes its speed to fill the new length. <kbd>⌥</kbd> on the start edge is an ordinary trim. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on either edge is a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).
412	
413	## What each edge does
414	
415	**A start trim** moves the clip's start and its place in the footage together. The frame under the edge stays put, and the rest of the clip stays where it is on the timeline.
416	
417	**An end trim** moves the clip's end. Nothing else about the clip changes.
418	
419	Neither trim moves the clips around it, so a trim leaves a gap or fills one. If you pull a clip over its neighbour, the overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule). Where it does, the later clip gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. Where it doesn't, a dragged edge waits at the last position that was allowed, and <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd> or a typed time beeps and changes nothing.
420	
421	## Trim to the playhead
422	
423	Select the clips, move the playhead inside them, then press <kbd>W</kbd> to trim their starts to the playhead or <kbd>E</kbd> to trim their ends. **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**, **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** and the matching buttons in the timeline bar do the same.
424	
425	Each selected clip the playhead is inside is trimmed, as one undo step: Trim Start for <kbd>W</kbd> and Trim End for <kbd>E</kbd>.
426	
427	When no selected clip crosses the playhead, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. The menu doesn't show <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> beside its items, but the buttons' tooltips name them.
428	
429	## Type a time
430	
431	Select one clip and open the **Timing** section of the Clip tab's **Clip** sub-tab. **In** is where the clip starts on the timeline and **Out** is where it ends. Typing a new time is the same trim as dragging that edge.
432	
433	A time past what the clip can reach lands at the limit, and the field shows where it went. See [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/).
434	
435	## How far a trim goes
436	
437	A clip always keeps at least one frame.
438	
439	A media clip's trim stops at the start and end of its file. The end stops on the last whole frame the file still holds. A [slip or a roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) can't pass either end of the file either.
440	
441	Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics, adjustment clips and nests have no file length, so they trim to any length. A trimmed [nest](/editing/nests/) cuts nothing inside it. Trimming its end hides the tail. A nest always plays from its own first frame, so trimming its start moves what's inside along with the new start, rather than cutting into it.
442	
443	## What a trim keeps
444	
445	- **Linked sound.** Trim a picture and its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) follows, if the two edges matched and the sound's track isn't locked. Trim the sound half and it goes alone, which is how you make a [J-cut or an L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> work the same way. The **In** and **Out** fields always take a matching partner along, whichever half you selected.
446	- **Actions.** They keep their time from the clip's start, so they stay put relative to the new start. An action past a new end is kept, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
447	- **Caption words.** Timed words stay on their speech.
448	- **Speed ramps.** On a [ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after a new start can change. The start stops where the clip still fits its media.
449	
450	## Trim a graphic
451	
452	Trimming the front of a graphic clip cuts into its animation. The **In** row of the **Timeline** section in the **Graphic** sub-tab moves forward, and the outro keeps its timing. That **In** counts the graphic's own frames, so it isn't the **In** field under **Timing**.
453	
454	A graphic has no file to run out of, so you can also drag its start back earlier. The graphic's **In** stops at 0, and the clip keeps growing.
455	
456	Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the clip's new end. A clip longer than a pinned **Length** keeps drawing frames past it, with its progress held at the end. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
457	
458	## With an agent
459	
460	[`trim_start`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start) and [`trim_end`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_end) move an edge to a time you give them. With `alone`, they trim either half of a linked pair on its own. On the timeline, only the sound half trims alone. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
461

470	---
471	title: "Type a clip's timing"
472	description: "Trim a clip to an exact time by typing its In and Out, and read its length, in the Clip tab's Timing section."
473	---
474	
475	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
476	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
477	
478	The Timing section is for when you know the number. Type where a clip starts and ends on the timeline, and read how long it is, without dragging an edge.
479	
480	<AtAGlance
481	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing"
482	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
483	/>
484	
485	## Type In and Out
486	
487	<Steps>
488	
489	1. Select one clip.
490	
491	2. In the [inspector's](/getting-started/inspector/) **Clip** tab, choose the **Clip** sub-tab, the last one. **Timing** is its first section, and it starts shut. Click its header to open it, and it stays open until you shut it. Shut, the header still shows the clip's length.
492	
493	3. Click **In** or **Out** and type a time. `1:23`, `83.5` and `1:23:04` all work, as they do in the toolbar's time field. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).
494	
495	4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>.
496	
497	</Steps>
498	
499	| Field | What it is | What typing does |
500	| --- | --- | --- |
501	| **In** | Where the clip starts on the timeline | Trims its front edge. The rest of the clip stays where it is. |
502	| **Out** | Where the clip ends on the timeline | Trims its back edge. |
503	
504	Both are positions on the timeline, not positions in the file. A later **In** hides the start of the footage, and an earlier one brings it back. To move the whole clip without trimming it, [drag it](/editing/move-clips/) instead.
505	
506	Each change is one undo step, named Trim Start or Trim End. The time lands on the project's frame grid.
507	
508	## How far an edge can go
509	
510	A number out of range doesn't beep. The edge goes as far as it can, and the field shows where it landed.
511	
512	| Field | Earliest | Latest |
513	| --- | --- | --- |
514	| **In** | The start of the timeline, or as far back as the file has footage | One frame before the clip's end |
515	| **Out** | One frame after the clip's start | As far as the file has footage |
516	
517	Only a clip that plays a video or audio file has a footage limit. Text, shapes, pictures and graphics have no file length to run out of.
518	
519	Three things leave the clip as it was:
520	
521	- If you type a new value but it puts the edge where it already is, Frame Job beeps.
522	- If the text can't be read as a time, Frame Job beeps and the field goes back to the old value.
523	- If the new edge would break the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.
524	
525	An overlap the rule allows goes through, and the clip that now overlaps the one before it gets a Cross Dissolve.
526	
527	## Read the duration
528	
529	**Duration** shows the clip's length, in the project's [timecode style](/projects/background-and-timecode/). You can't type in it: change the length through **In** and **Out**.
530	
531	## With several clips selected
532	
533	**In**, **Out** and **Duration** each describe one clip, so they go away when you select more than one.
534	
535	If every selected clip plays a video or audio file, Timing stays and holds only the [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) rows, which apply to all of them as one undo step. Its header shows the lengths of the selected clips added together, followed by "total".
536	
537	If the selection also holds anything else, such as text, a shape, a picture or a freeze frame, there's no Timing section.
538	
539	## Good to know
540	
541	- With one clip selected, the Reverse rows appear under **Duration** only for a clip that plays a video or audio file.
542	- Typing an edge also moves the same edge of a [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) when the two line up and its track isn't locked. That holds even when you type on the sound half. To move a sound's edge without its picture, [use a drag, <kbd>W</kbd> or <kbd>E</kbd>](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone).
543	- A locked track stops drags, not these fields. If a clip on a locked track is selected, typing still trims it.
544	- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the times count from the nest's own start.
545	- [Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) keep their place measured from the clip's start, so trimming the front edge moves them along the timeline with it.
546	
547	## With an agent
548	
549	[`trim_start`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start) and [`trim_end`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_end) move the same two edges to a time on the timeline, and stop at the same limits. With `alone`, the edge moves without its linked partner's. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
550

557	=================== slip-and-roll
558	---
559	title: "Slip and roll"
560	description: "Change which footage a clip shows, or move the cut between two clips, without moving anything else on the timeline."
561	---
562	
563	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
564	
565	Slip and roll are for fine-tuning once your clips are where they belong. A slip changes which part of the file a clip shows. A roll moves the cut between two clips. Neither moves any other clip.
566	
567	<AtAGlance
568	  keys={['⌥⇧-drag body', '⌥⇧-drag edge']}
569	  where="The timeline"
570	  tools={['slip', 'roll', 'trim_start', 'trim_end']}
571	/>
572	
573	## Slip a clip
574	
575	Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the body of a clip. The clip stays where it is at the same length, and the footage slides underneath it. Drag right to show later footage and left to show earlier footage.
576	
577	The whole drag is one undo step, named Slip. It doesn't change the selection, so you can slip a clip without selecting it.
578	
579	- A slip stops when the clip reaches either end of its file, and keeps what it reached. It doesn't turn into a trim. If there's no footage to slide into, the drag changes nothing.
580	- It moves in whole frames and never snaps, because the timeline's snap points mean nothing inside the footage.
581	- The footage moves at the clip's speed. At ×2, dragging one frame slides the footage two frames.
582	- A [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) slips too, which changes the frame it holds. It stops one frame short of the end of its file.
583	- A linked sound clip on an unlocked track slips with its picture, so the two stay in sync. They move by the smaller of the two distances they each have room for.
584	
585	Only clips that play a file have footage to slide. The drag does nothing on text, a shape, a picture, a graphic or a nest.
586	
587	## Roll a cut
588	
589	Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag a clip's edge, the outer 7 points of the clip. The cut moves: one clip gets longer and the other gets shorter by the same amount, and the outer edges of the pair stay where they are.
590	
591	| Edge you drag | Cut that moves |
592	| --- | --- |
593	| The clip's start | The cut with the clip before it |
594	| The clip's end | The cut with the clip after it |
595	
596	The whole drag is one undo step, named Roll.
597	
598	- A roll [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like a trim. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to stop snapping.
599	- Each clip keeps at least one frame.
600	- A clip that plays a file can't grow past what the file has. Text, shapes and pictures have no such limit.
601	- A roll needs two clips that touch exactly. With a gap at that edge there's no cut to move, and with an overlap there's a [transition](/motion/transition-settings/), whose length you set in its own section. Either way the drag does nothing.
602	- A clip 21 points wide or less on screen has no edges to grab, and the drag slips it instead. [Zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) first.
603	
604	When you roll a picture's cut, a linked sound clip rolls with it, as long as it starts at the same point, it touches a clip before it, and its track is unlocked.
605	
606	## Move a sound clip's edge alone
607	
608	A [detached sound clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) that's still linked to its picture can move an edge on its own. This is how a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) is made. These move only the sound's edge and leave the picture where it is:
609	
610	- Drag the sound clip's edge.
611	- Select it and press <kbd>W</kbd> or <kbd>E</kbd> to [trim it to the playhead](/editing/trimming/).
612	- Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the sound clip's edge to roll its cut.
613	
614	It works in that direction only. Trimming or rolling the picture's edge also moves the sound's edge when the two line up, and a slip always takes both.
615	
616	## What happens to actions and timed words
617	
618	A slip leaves [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) where they are, because only the footage inside the clip moves.
619	
620	A roll leaves each clip's actions at the same distance from that clip's start. So on the clip after the cut, the actions move with the cut along the timeline. On the clip before it, they stay put, and if that clip gets shorter it can end before an action does.
621	
622	Timed caption words are the exception. They stay on the speech they time, so a roll doesn't shift them against the sound. A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) after the cut stays in step too: its **In** moves with the cut.
623	
624	## Good to know
625	
626	- Neither gesture works on a locked track. The drag does nothing. A linked clip on a locked track stays put while the clip you drag moves.
627	- On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the actions stay where they are and the limits come from the ramp, so a cut stops rolling where the clip would no longer fit its file.
628	
629	## With an agent
630	
631	[`slip`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#slip) takes a clip and how far to slide, and a positive distance shows later footage. Where the drag does nothing on text, a shape, a picture, a graphic or a nest, the tool gives an error.
632	
633	[`roll`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#roll) takes the clip to the right of the cut and the time the cut moves to. If no clip on the track ends where that clip begins, it gives an error saying so.
634	
635	With `alone`, `roll` moves a picture's cut and leaves a lined-up linked sound on an unlocked track where it is. No gesture can do that. [`trim_start`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start) and [`trim_end`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_end) take `alone` too, to move one clip's edge without its partner's. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).

643	=================== splitting
644	---
645	title: "Split clips"
646	description: "Cut clips in two at the playhead, and see what each piece keeps of the footage, actions, word timings and graphics."
647	---
648	
649	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
650	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
651	
652	Split cuts a clip in two at the playhead, so you can trim, move or remove one piece without touching the other.
653	
654	<AtAGlance
655	  menu="Clip ▸ Split"
656	  keys="⌘T"
657	  where="The scissors button in the timeline bar"
658	  tools="split"
659	/>
660	
661	## Split at the playhead
662	
663	<Steps>
664	
665	1. Move the playhead to the frame you want to cut on.
666	
667	2. Select the clips to cut, or select nothing to cut everything under the playhead.
668	
669	3. Press <kbd>⌘T</kbd>, choose **Clip ▸ Split**, or click the scissors button in the timeline bar.
670	
671	</Steps>
672	
673	| What's selected | What gets cut |
674	| --- | --- |
675	| One or more clips | Each selected clip the playhead is inside |
676	| Nothing | Every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track |
677	
678	It's one undo step, named Split, however many clips it cuts. The command is available whenever the timeline has clips.
679	
680	The playhead has to be strictly inside a clip. A playhead sitting exactly on a clip's edge is at a cut already, so that clip is left alone. If nothing can be cut, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.
681	
682	A clip on a locked track is left alone when nothing is selected, but it's still cut if you selected it.
683	
684	## Footage stays continuous
685	
686	The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped, at the same speed, so the split doesn't show when you play it back. If an action is animating the clip, the second piece starts from where that animation had got to at the cut, such as its position or volume. It keeps the clip's name, label and settings.
687	
688	On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the two pieces meet at exactly the same point in the footage, and the second starts at the rate in force at the cut.
689	
690	## Linked sound
691	
692	A [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) on an unlocked track is cut too, when the playhead is inside it, and the two second halves are linked to each other.
693	
694	If the linked clip isn't cut, because its track is locked or the playhead isn't inside it, it stays linked to whichever piece shares more of its time. The other piece isn't linked to anything.
695	
696	## Actions and word timings
697	
698	[Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) stay with the piece they fall in:
699	
700	- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first piece.
701	- An action that starts at or after the cut moves to the second piece.
702	- An action that spans the cut becomes two. The first half ends at the value it had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original target, so the join doesn't show. Both keep the action's curve.
703	
704	An [entrance and exit preset](/motion/entrances-and-exits/) is tied to the clip's ends, so the first piece keeps the entrance and the second keeps the exit. A [text reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) divides the same way. Otherwise the clip would leave at the cut and arrive again on the far side of it.
705	
706	Caption word timings stay on their words. Both pieces keep the full text, the first with its timings as they were and the second with its timings moved to match its new start.
707	
708	The one exception is a text clip whose wording an action changes. If the second piece's text at the cut no longer has the same number of words as its timings, the second piece loses its word timings and shows its text all at once.
709	
710	## Split a graphic
711	
712	A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) carries on across the cut rather than starting again, and plays its outro once, at the true end.
713	
714	The graphic's **In** on the second piece starts at the cut, so it picks up where the first piece left off. Both pieces keep the original's **Length**, so an outro still plays at the same moment. That pins the length, so **Follow Clip** is off on both pieces afterwards.
715	
716	Trimming the start of a graphic, or [rolling the cut](/editing/slip-and-roll/#roll-a-cut) before it, moves **In** in the same way. Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the new end.
717	
718	## Good to know
719	
720	- The cut lands on the project's frame grid.
721	- A [transition](/motion/transitions/) into the clip stays on the first piece. The second piece starts with a hard cut.
722	- [Sound fades](/audio/fades/) are copied to both pieces. A clip with a fade-in fades in again at the cut, and one with a fade-out dips at the cut, so set them again on the side of the cut where you don't want them.
723	- A project holds up to 4,096 clips. A split that would pass that shows an error alert, and nothing changes.
724	
725	## With an agent
726	
727	`split` cuts at a time you give it, or at the playhead if you leave the time out. Give it a list of clips to cut those, or leave the list out to cut every clip on an unlocked track at that time, as the menu item does with nothing selected. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split).
728

735	=================== split-at-shot-changes
736	---
737	title: "Split at Shot Changes"
738	description: "Cut a finished edit, a download or a stream recording into one clip per shot, with the cuts found on your Mac."
739	---
740	
741	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
742	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
743	
744	Split at Shot Changes takes a clip that already has cuts in it, such as a finished edit, a downloaded clip or a stream recording, and cuts it at each one, giving you one clip per shot.
745	
746	<AtAGlance
747	  menu="Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes"
748	  tools={['split_at_shots', 'get_media_analysis']}
749	  needs="Nothing. The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
750	/>
751	
752	## Split a clip at its shot changes
753	
754	<Steps>
755	
756	1. Select one or more clips that show a video file's picture.
757	
758	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. It has no shortcut.
759	
760	3. If Frame Job hasn't looked at this footage yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#while-the-cuts-are-found) to finish.
761	
762	</Steps>
763	
764	Each selected clip is cut at every hard cut inside the part of the file it plays. All the cuts are one undo step, named Split at Shot Changes.
765	
766	The command is greyed out until a selected clip shows a video file's picture. Anything else in the selection is left alone: text, an image, a freeze frame, an audio file, a nest, or a clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
767	
768	If the footage holds no shot change inside any selected clip, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.
769	
770	## While the cuts are found
771	
772	When the footage has already been read, the split lands at once. Otherwise the **Analyzing** sheet appears, with one row per file:
773	
774	| A file's row reads | What it means |
775	| --- | --- |
776	| Waiting | Its first frame hasn't been read yet. |
777	| A percentage, with a bar | How much has been read. |
778	| Done | Its cuts have been found. |
779	
780	The split lands as soon as every file is done. Editing commands are off while the sheet is up.
781	
782	**Stop** closes the sheet and changes nothing. Frame Job saves what it has found every 30 seconds or so, and that stays in the cache, so a long file doesn't start from nothing next time.
783	
784	If the project changes anyway while the sheet is up, for example through an agent, nothing is split, and the inspector says to choose the command again.
785	
786	## What counts as a hard cut
787	
788	A hard cut is a change from one picture to another between two frames. Frame Job compares each frame's colours with those of the frames before it. It's a plain measurement of the picture, with no machine learning, so the same footage always gives the same cuts.
789	
790	- A gradual dissolve isn't a cut.
791	- A single flash frame isn't a cut, because the picture after it matches the one before.
792	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can be found as one cut.
793	- Two shots with very similar colours can be missed, because the comparison looks at colour rather than at what's in the frame.
794	- Of two cuts within 12 frames of each other in the file, only the stronger is found.
795	
796	## Found on this Mac and cached
797	
798	Shot changes are found on your Mac. Nothing is sent anywhere and you don't need a key.
799	
800	The results are kept in the project's cache, so a second split of the same footage starts at once. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).
801	
802	## Where the cuts land
803	
804	Each cut lands on the project's frame grid, worked out through the clip's speed, [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) and [reversal](/speed/reverse/). In a project whose frame rate differs from the file's, that's the nearest project frame.
805	
806	A cut within one frame of either end of a clip isn't made, so you won't get a piece one frame long at a clip's edge.
807	
808	Each cut is an ordinary [split](/editing/splitting/), so actions, word timings and graphics divide the same way.
809	
810	## Locked tracks and linked sound
811	
812	A selected clip on a locked track is still cut. Its linked sound is cut with it when the sound's track is unlocked, as with [Split](/editing/splitting/#linked-sound).
813	
814	## The clip ceiling
815	
816	A project holds up to 4,096 clips, counting the clips inside nests. If the splits would pass that, nothing is split at all, and the inspector says how many clips the command would add and how many more would fit. The count includes each linked clip the splits also cut.
817	
818	## When it can't run
819	
820	Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector:
821	
822	| What happened | What to do |
823	| --- | --- |
824	| A file is missing or can't be read | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), then choose the command again. |
825	| The analysis of a file failed | The message names the file and the reason. Nothing is split. |
826	| The analysis is no longer in the project's cache | Choose the command again, and Frame Job reads the file again. |
827	
828	## With an agent
829	
830	`split_at_shots` works on the clips it's given, and lists any it can't cut under `skipped`. Without a list, it takes every clip of a video file on an unlocked track, so a clip on a locked track is cut only when it's named. It shows no sheet. It waits up to 60 seconds for the cuts, and if they aren't ready it stops without splitting and keeps what it has saved so far, so calling it again carries on.
831	
832	With no cut inside any clip, it reports that no clips were added and leaves no undo step. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split_at_shots).
833	
834	[`get_media_analysis`](/mcp/tools-analysis/#get_media_analysis), with the kind `shots`, reads a file's cuts without splitting anything. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
835

1	=================== delete-clips
2	---
3	title: "Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift"
4	description: "Remove clips or a stretch of the timeline, and choose whether the hole stays open or closes up."
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	There are two delete keys, and the difference between them is what happens to the hole. <kbd>⌫</kbd> leaves it open, so everything else keeps its timing. <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> closes it, so the rest of the timeline moves left.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
13	  keys={['⌫', '⌘⌫']}
14	  where="The Ripple Delete button in the timeline bar"
15	  tools={['delete', 'ripple_delete', 'lift_range', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
16	/>
17	
18	## Choose a delete
19	
20	Each key acts on the selection, or on the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when nothing is selected.
21	
22	| | Clips selected | Nothing selected, a range set |
23	| --- | --- | --- |
24	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Delete** | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** removes what's in the range and moves nothing. |
25	| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips and closes each hole. | **Ripple Delete:** removes what's in the range and closes the hole. |
26	
27	A selection takes priority over a range, so [deselect](/timeline/selecting-clips/) first to act on the range. An empty range is ignored. With nothing to remove, both menu items are greyed out and the keys beep.
28	
29	## Delete clips and leave a gap
30	
31	Select the clips and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. They go, the gaps stay, and nothing else moves. It's one undo step, named Delete.
32	
33	- A picture takes its [linked sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) with it, unless the sound's track is locked.
34	- A linked sound clip goes alone, and leaves its picture silent.
35	- A clip on a locked track that you selected by clicking is still removed.
36	
37	## Ripple delete clips
38	
39	Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, or use the timeline bar's button. The clips go, and each hole closes: everything later on every unlocked track moves left. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.
40	
41	- Each clip's linked partner on an unlocked track goes too, whichever half you selected.
42	- A clip on a locked track that you selected is removed, but clips on locked tracks don't move.
43	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.
44	
45	:::caution
46	Unlike <kbd>⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> ignores a [selected action](/motion/select-an-action/). With an action selected it ripple-deletes the whole clip. Undo brings it back.
47	:::
48	
49	## Lift a range
50	
51	Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, and what lies between is removed. Nothing moves, markers included. It's one undo step, named Lift.
52	
53	Lift is the safe cut when a mix or a caption track is already timed, because everything after the range keeps its moment. Clips on locked tracks are neither cut nor removed. If the range held nothing to remove, Frame Job beeps.
54	
55	## Ripple delete a range
56	
57	Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, what lies between is removed, and the hole closes. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.
58	
59	Clips on locked tracks are neither cut, removed nor moved, even inside the range. Everything else after the range moves left by its length, so a locked track falls out of step with the rest. That's what the lock is for.
60	
61	## How a ripple closes holes
62	
63	Each hole closes with one shift of everything after it, so clips that touched before still touch.
64	
65	- A clip past several holes moves by their combined length. Two removed clips that touch leave one hole.
66	- A clip moves if it starts at or after the end of the hole. When you ripple-delete clips, a clip on another track that spans the hole stays where it is, and isn't shortened.
67	- A clip's linked partner on an unlocked track moves with it.
68	- Markers stay at their times, because a marker inside a removed stretch would have nowhere to go.
69	- A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. A ripple is never stopped by the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
70	
71	One thing does stop a ripple. If it would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline, as a sound leading its picture in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) can, nothing moves, and the foot of the inspector names both clips.
72	
73	## Ripple delete several ranges
74	
75	An agent can cut a list of time ranges out of the timeline as one edit and one undo step, with [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges). It shows as Ripple Delete under **Edit ▸ Undo**. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) make the same cut from their sheets.
76	
77	Ranges that touch or overlap merge into one before anything is cut, so two ranges that meet leave one hole, and all the cuts use times from the timeline as it was before the edit. Each range then behaves as [a ripple-deleted range](#ripple-delete-a-range) does: locked tracks are left alone and markers don't move. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).
78	
79	## When the delete keys do something else
80	
81	<kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the first of these it finds:
82	
83	1. Words or a pause selected in the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/), while that tab has the focus. They ripple out and the gap closes, as deleting text does.
84	2. A [selected action](/motion/change-an-action/). The action goes and its clip stays.
85	3. The selected clips.
86	4. The in/out range.
87	
88	<kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> follows the same order without the second step.
89	
90	While you type in a text field, both menu items are greyed out, so <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> edit the text. That covers the timecode fields, a rename and a text clip.
91	
92	While a point is selected in a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point and **Edit ▸ Delete** is greyed out.
93	
94	## With an agent
95	
96	[`delete`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#delete) and [`ripple_delete`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete) take a list of clips. [`lift_range`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#lift_range) and [`ripple_delete_range`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_range) take a start and an end time, `from` and `to`, and `to` has to be after `from`. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

105	=================== close-gaps
106	---
107	title: "Close gaps and insert time"
108	description: "Close an empty stretch of a track with a double-click or Close Gap, and open room on the timeline when you need it."
109	---
110	
111	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
112	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
113	
114	Closing a gap pulls everything after it back to meet what's before it, on every unlocked track, so the timeline stays in sync. Opening room does the opposite.
115	
116	<AtAGlance
117	  menu="Clip ▸ Close Gap"
118	  where="Double-click an empty stretch of a lane"
119	  tools={['close_gap', 'insert_time']}
120	/>
121	
122	## Double-click a gap
123	
124	Double-click an empty stretch of a track's lane. Everything after the gap, on every unlocked track, moves left by the gap's length. It's one undo step, named Close Gap.
125	
126	This only works on a lane. Above the first lane or below the last there's no track, so there's nothing to close.
127	
128	## Close the gap under the playhead
129	
130	Move the playhead into a gap and choose **Clip ▸ Close Gap**. It has no shortcut.
131	
132	It works on the current track: the selected clip's track or, with nothing selected, the front track. The result is the same as a double-click. The command is available when the timeline has clips.
133	
134	## What moves
135	
136	- A gap is the empty stretch between two clips on that track. A gap before the first clip closes back to the start of the timeline.
137	- Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after the far side of the gap moves left. A clip on another track that spans that point stays where it is.
138	- A moved clip's [linked partner](/audio/detach-and-attach/) moves too, when its track is unlocked.
139	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.
140	- A clip that ends up overlapping the one before it, within the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), gets a Cross Dissolve.
141	
142	## When a gap won't close
143	
144	A gap closes completely or not at all. Frame Job beeps, moves nothing and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector when:
145	
146	| What's wrong | What to do |
147	| --- | --- |
148	| The playhead is on a clip, not in a gap | Move the playhead into the gap, or check the current track. |
149	| No clip follows the gap on that track | There's nothing to pull back. |
150	| The track is locked | [Unlock it](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). Its clips are the ones that would stay behind. |
151	| Closing it would push clips into an overlap the overlap rule forbids, on any track that moves | Trim or move those clips first. |
152	| A linked clip would go before the start of the timeline | Happens when a sound leads its picture, as in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). Trim the front of the sound so it leads by less. |
153	
154	## Insert time
155	
156	Inserting time opens empty room. Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later by a length, and so does every marker at or after that point, unlike a ripple.
157	
158	Clips that span the point stay put, so nothing is cut. To open room inside a clip, [split](/editing/splitting/) it first.
159	
160	Inserting time has no menu item or gesture of its own. An ⌥-drop [insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) and [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) both do it as part of their edit, and an agent can do it directly.
161	
162	## Open room by hand
163	
164	<Steps>
165	
166	1. Move the playhead to where the room should start.
167	
168	2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd> (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**) to select every clip that starts at or after the playhead.
169	
170	3. Drag the selected clips later, or press <kbd>⇧.</kbd> to [nudge](/editing/nudge-clips/) them 10 frames at a time.
171	
172	</Steps>
173	
174	This differs from inserting time in two ways: it also moves the selected clips on locked tracks, and it leaves markers where they are. Start the drag on a clip on an unlocked track, because a clip on a locked track can't be grabbed.
175	
176	## With an agent
177	
178	[`close_gap`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#close_gap) takes a track and a time inside the gap, and stops for the same reasons as the menu item. [`insert_time`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#insert_time) takes the point to open room at and how much room to open. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).
179

186	=================== duplicate-clips
187	---
188	title: Duplicate clips
189	description: Put copies of the selected clips straight after them with one key, or drag copies to exactly where you want them.
190	---
191	
192	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
193	
194	Duplicate makes copies of clips without going through the clipboard. Press a key to put them right after the originals, or hold ⌥ and drag them where you want them.
195	
196	<AtAGlance
197	  menu="Edit ▸ Duplicate"
198	  keys={['⌘D', '⌥-drag']}
199	  where="The Duplicate button in the timeline bar"
200	  tools={['duplicate', 'move_clip']}
201	/>
202	
203	## Duplicate the selection
204	
205	Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. **Edit ▸ Duplicate** and the timeline bar's **Duplicate** button do the same. With nothing selected, the menu item is greyed out and the button beeps.
206	
207	The button sits in the [timeline bar](/getting-started/editor-window/#timeline-bar) with the other one-click clip tools, which split, trim, ripple delete and add markers, text and shapes.
208	
209	Each copy goes on the same track as its original, starting right after the selection's span. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing: if it runs from 10 s to 14 s, every copy starts 4 s later than its original.
210	
211	The copies are one undo step, called Duplicate.
212	
213	## Drag a copy
214	
215	To place copies somewhere else, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press on a clip, then drag. The copies follow the pointer and the originals stay where they are.
216	
217	- If the clip you press is part of the selection, the whole selection is copied. If it isn't, only that clip is.
218	- The copies snap and change tracks as a [move](/editing/move-clips/) does. Drop past the top or bottom of the stack to make a new track for them.
219	- A spot the timeline can't take is skipped. The copies stay at the last spot along the drag that worked, and if none did, nothing changes.
220	- The whole drag is one undo step, called Duplicate Clips.
221	
222	Hold only <kbd>⌥</kbd>. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on a clip is a [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/), not a copy.
223	
224	:::caution
225	An ⌥-drag makes its copies by duplicating first, so it needs the room a <kbd>⌘D</kbd> would need. If Duplicate [wouldn't work](#when-duplicate-wont-work) at that moment, because the next clip is hard up against the selection, the drag moves the originals instead. Undo it, then [copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) the clip, which has no such limit.
226	:::
227	
228	## What a copy keeps
229	
230	A copy is the whole clip: its source, trim, speed, name, label, picture and sound settings, and actions. From then on it's a clip of its own, so changing one doesn't change the other.
231	
232	- **Linked clips.** If a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), its partner is copied too and the two copies are linked to each other. A partner on a locked track isn't copied.
233	- **Nest clips.** A copy of a nest clip made with Duplicate or ⌥-drag shows the same nest as the original, so an edit inside one shows in both. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).
234	
235	## When Duplicate won't work
236	
237	Copies follow the same [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) as any other placement, and Frame Job doesn't push later clips out of the way.
238	
239	- A copy may overlap the clip after it by up to half of the shorter clip. The overlap gets a Cross Dissolve, as any new overlap does. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
240	- A longer overlap stops the duplicate. Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
241	- An adjustment clip can't overlap anything, so a copy of one needs clear space.
242	
243	To duplicate into a tight edit, open room first or use **Edit ▸ Copy** and **Edit ▸ Paste**. A paste that has no room goes on a new track.
244	
245	## With an agent
246	
247	`duplicate` takes the clips to copy and puts the copies straight after them, as <kbd>⌘D</kbd> does. There's no agent version of an ⌥-drag: follow `duplicate` with [`move_clip`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip) to put the copies somewhere else. Both also work inside a nest. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#duplicate).
248
