255	=================== copy-and-paste
256	---
257	title: Copy, cut and paste
258	description: Copy clips to the clipboard and paste them at the playhead, in the same project or another one, keeping their arrangement.
259	---
260	
261	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
262	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
263	
264	The clipboard carries clips from one place to another: later in the same timeline, or into a different project. Pasted clips land at the playhead and keep the arrangement you copied.
265	
266	<AtAGlance
267	  menu={['Edit ▸ Copy', 'Edit ▸ Cut', 'Edit ▸ Paste']}
268	  keys={['⌘C', '⌘X', '⌘V']}
269	  tools="paste"
270	/>
271	
272	## Copy and paste clips
273	
274	<Steps>
275	
276	1. Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Copy**. The clipboard holds the clips and a note of the media files they show.
277	
278	2. Move the playhead to where they should go.
279	
280	3. Press <kbd>⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste**.
281	
282	</Steps>
283	
284	The pasted clips are selected, so you can drag or style them straight away. The paste is one undo step, called Paste, and you can paste the same clips as many times as you like.
285	
286	**Copy** and **Cut** are greyed out with nothing selected. **Paste** needs no selection. It's greyed out unless Frame Job clips are on the clipboard, because it never pastes another app's text or files.
287	
288	While you're typing in a field, these keys act on the text in the field, not on clips.
289	
290	## Cut clips
291	
292	Press <kbd>⌘X</kbd> or choose **Edit ▸ Cut**. The clips go on the clipboard and are then deleted, leaving gaps, exactly as <kbd>⌫</kbd> does. To close the gaps as well, see [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).
293	
294	A cut is one undo step, called Cut. If the clips can't be copied, Frame Job beeps and deletes nothing.
295	
296	## Where pasted clips land
297	
298	Paste keeps the arrangement you copied.
299	
300	- **In time.** The earliest clip lands at the playhead, and every other clip keeps its distance from it. Everything lands on a frame.
301	- **Across tracks.** Each clip keeps its place in the stack, counted back from the front. A clip copied from the front track lands on the front track, and one copied from the second track down lands on the second track down. A selection across two lanes pastes back onto two lanes.
302	- **Missing tracks.** If the project has too few tracks, new ones are added at the back.
303	
304	## When there's no room
305	
306	A paste isn't turned down for lack of room. A clip that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) on its track goes on a new track at the front, so it stays visible over what was already there.
307	
308	A smaller overlap is allowed, as it is for any placement: up to half of the shorter clip. The clip stays on its track and the overlap gets a Cross Dissolve. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
309	
310	## Paste into another project
311	
312	Copy in one project, switch to another and paste. The clips stay on the clipboard, so the other project can be opened before or after you copy.
313	
314	- **Media.** Files are matched by their path. A file the project already has is reused, and one it doesn't have is added to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/), with the same checks an import makes. Only files the pasted clips use come across, including the `.cube` file of a [look](/color/luts/) and the LUT of [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
315	- **Frame rate.** Pasted clips are snapped to this project's frame rate.
316	- **New clips.** What lands is a new set of clips, so you can paste them again into the project they came from.
317	
318	A graphic clip brings its name and not its files. In a project without that graphic, the clip draws a red error card until you add a graphic of the same name. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
319	
320	## A detached sound comes along
321	
322	When a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), selecting its picture copies both, so the pair pastes as a linked pair. Selecting the sound on its own copies only the sound, and it pastes as an ordinary clip with no link to any picture.
323	
324	Cut follows the same split. Cutting a picture takes its sound with it, unless the sound is on a locked track. Cutting a detached sound on its own leaves the picture in place, silent.
325	
326	## Copied clips as text
327	
328	Paste into a text editor and you get a one-line summary of what was copied, in the project's timecode:
329	
330	```text
331	Frame Job — 2 clips, 00:00:01:00 to 00:00:04:00
332	```
333	
334	## Good to know
335	
336	:::caution
337	**Nest clips can't be pasted.** The clipboard holds the nest clip but not what's inside it, so **Paste** shows an error and pastes nothing, even if only one of the copied clips is a nest clip. **Cut** still deletes a nest clip, so press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> to bring it back. To make another copy of a nest clip, use [Duplicate or ⌥-drag](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
338	:::
339	
340	- A paste lands whole or not at all. If one clip can't go in, Frame Job shows an error naming it and nothing changes. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), for example, can't be pasted while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open.
341	- Room for a paste isn't unlimited: a project holds up to 64 tracks and 4,096 clips. A paste that would pass either limit shows an error.
342	- Copy and Paste work inside a nest. **Copy** takes the clips you picked and counts their depth against the nest's own tracks, and **Paste** lands in the nest that's open.
343	
344	## With an agent
345	
346	`paste` takes a description of the clips in the same form Copy writes, so an agent can place clips without touching your clipboard. `at` sets the time, the playhead if it's left out, and `track` sets where the front-most copied lane lands, the front track if it's left out. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste).
347	
348	## Related
349	
350	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
351	- [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/)
352	- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
353	- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
354	=================== paste-attributes
355	---
356	title: Paste Attributes
357	description: Copy one clip's look and sound settings onto any number of other clips in a single step.
358	---
359	
360	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
361	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
362	
363	Paste Attributes makes other clips look and sound like the one you copied. Set up one clip, then give the same settings to the rest in one undo step.
364	
365	<AtAGlance
366	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
367	  keys="⌥⌘V"
368	  tools="paste_attributes"
369	/>
370	
371	## Paste a clip's attributes
372	
373	<Steps>
374	
375	1. Select the clip that has the settings you want and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
376	
377	2. Select the clips that should take them.
378	
379	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
380	
381	</Steps>
382	
383	The item is available when Frame Job clips are on the clipboard and something is selected. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps. The paste is one undo step, called Paste Attributes.
384	
385	If you copied several clips, only one of them counts: the one that starts earliest. At the same start it's the one on the front-most track.
386	
387	## What travels
388	
389	Settings travel in four groups, and a group is only copied when both clips have it. A movie's settings pasted onto a text clip bring its picture settings and leave the text styling alone, and its sound settings go nowhere.
390	
391	Each group replaces the target's whole group, so it isn't a merge. A shadow on the target disappears if the copied clip had none.
392	
393	| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
394	| --- | --- | --- |
395	| **Video** | Everything about the picture: position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corner radius, blend mode, shadow, reflection, filters, spotlight, obscure regions, chroma key, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, Hide While Silent, motion presets, motion blur, the grade and its look, and the [drawn cursor's](/recording/cursor-settings/) settings | Nothing, apart from an adjustment clip's [qualifier](#adjustment-clips-and-qualifiers) |
396	| **Audio** | Everything about the sound: volume, Mute, fades and their shapes, pan, Mix to mono, channels, Keep pitch, ducking, noise reduction, voice isolation, EQ, hum removal, gate, de-esser, leveller, compressor, limiter and voice effects | Nothing |
397	| **Text** | Font, size, colours, alignment, spacing, case, outline, backdrop, text box width, reveal animation and word caption style | Its own words and their timings |
398	| **Shape** | Fill, stroke, gradient, corner radius and arrowheads | Its kind, its size and the end points of a line |
399	
400	:::caution
401	The Video group includes position and scale. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits.
402	:::
403	
404	A look's `.cube` file comes along too, so a grade pasted from another project keeps its LUT.
405	
406	## What stays on the target
407	
408	Paste Attributes copies how a clip looks and sounds, not what makes it that clip. The target keeps:
409	
410	- its place on the timeline and its length
411	- its speed, including a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/)
412	- its [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/), so nothing animated travels
413	- its transition
414	- its name and label
415	- which halves are [switched on](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/)
416	
417	Graphic properties don't travel either. Use [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/) for those.
418	
419	## Adjustment clips and qualifiers
420	
421	A qualifier belongs to an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), so it follows the kind of clip:
422	
423	| Pasting | The qualifier |
424	| --- | --- |
425	| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
426	| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
427	| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |
428	
429	See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/) for moving a grade between clips.
430	
431	## When a paste stops
432	
433	Some picture settings can't land on some kinds of clip. When one can't, Frame Job shows an error saying why and changes nothing, even on the other selected clips.
434	
435	| The target | Can't take |
436	| --- | --- |
437	| An adjustment clip | Blur, sharpen or pixelate filters, a blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
438	| A nest clip | A blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur, Hide While Silent |
439	| A text, shape or graphic clip | Remove Background |
440	| A movie clip or freeze frame | Remove Background with its subject set to Foreground, which only an image clip can take |
441	| Any clip except a text or adjustment clip | A crop that would leave nothing of it, such as one copied from a much larger source |
442	
443	To get past one, take the setting off the copied clip, copy it again and paste, or select only the clips that can take it.
444	
445	## With an agent
446	
447	`paste_attributes` can do two things the menu item can't.
448	
449	- **Choose the groups.** `groups` names which ones travel, out of `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape` and `graphic`, so `["audio"]` pastes the sound alone and leaves the picture settings. Left out, it behaves as the menu item does, and `graphic` only travels when it's named. An empty list won't run.
450	- **Skip what doesn't fit.** A named group that either side lacks normally stops the paste with an error. With `skip_missing` on, a group the copied clip lacks is dropped and a clip that can't take a group is skipped, so a mixed selection goes through. It's off by default, and only applies with `groups`.
451	
452	See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste_attributes).
453	
454	## Related
455	
456	- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
457	- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
458	- [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/)
459	- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
460	=================== enable-picture-and-sound
461	---
462	title: Turn a clip's picture or sound off
463	description: What it means when one half of a clip is switched off, which commands do it, and how the clip then looks on the timeline.
464	---
465	
466	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
467	
468	A clip has two halves, its picture and its sound, and each can be switched off while the clip stays where it is. A switched-off half adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and it comes back when the half is switched on again.
469	
470	<AtAGlance
471	  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
472	  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
473	  tools="set_enabled"
474	/>
475	
476	## Turn a half off
477	
478	There's no switch for this in the inspector. Commands flip the halves as part of what they do:
479	
480	| Command | What it switches |
481	| --- | --- |
482	| [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Turns the clip's sound off and adds a sound-only copy on the track below, with its picture off. |
483	| [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Merges a detached pair back into one clip with its sound on. |
484	| [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Can turn off the picture of the camera clips it replaces, and their sound when **Mute the cameras' own sound** is ticked. |
485	
486	To silence a clip's sound by hand, use **Mute** on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To hide its picture, set its [opacity](/canvas/transform/) to 0 or [hide the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
487	
488	## How the clip looks
489	
490	| Switched off | On the timeline |
491	| --- | --- |
492	| The picture of a movie clip | It reads as an audio clip, with the audio tint and symbol, and has no filmstrip. |
493	| The sound | It has no waveform. |
494	| Both | It's dimmed, like a clip on a hidden track. |
495	
496	A clip with its sound off has no **Sound** tab in the inspector, because there's nothing there to adjust. Its **Picture** tab stays, even with the picture off.
497	
498	## Good to know
499	
500	- A clip with its sound off can't be transcribed, and **Remove Silences** doesn't count it as audible.
501	- Copies keep the switches of the clip they came from.
502	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) leaves the target's switches alone.
503	
504	## With an agent
505	
506	`set_enabled` switches either half of any clip directly, which no command in the app does on its own. Give it `video`, `audio` or both, as true or false, and a half you leave out stays as it is. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#set_enabled).
507	
508	## Related
509	
510	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
511	- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
512	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
513	=================== nests
514	---
515	title: Nests
516	description: Collapse several clips into one clip that moves, trims, fades and transforms as a group, and open it back out when you're done.
517	---
518	
519	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
520	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
521	
522	A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing, and the clips inside stay as you built them.
523	
524	<AtAGlance
525	  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
526	  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
527	  tools={['nest', 'unnest', 'set_clip']}
528	/>
529	
530	## Make a nest
531	
532	<Steps>
533	
534	1. Select the clips.
535	
536	2. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.
537	
538	</Steps>
539	
540	The clips are replaced by one nest clip, which is selected so you can move or transform it straight away. The nest is one undo step, called Nest.
541	
542	The nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end, including any gaps. A matte track is the exception: the nest clip goes on the front-most track that isn't a matte, and a matte only stays one inside the nest if the track it cuts goes in with it. See [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/).
543	
544	A clip's [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) goes in with it, unless the sound is on a locked track.
545	
546	To work on the contents later, double-click the nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/).
547	
548	## What a nest keeps
549	
550	Inside the nest, clips keep their properties, [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) and transitions, their timing relative to each other and their stacking order. The earliest clip starts at 0 on the nest's own timeline.
551	
552	The tracks inside are new, and each keeps the name, the hidden, muted, locked and solo states, and the volume and pan of the track it came from. There are two exceptions:
553	
554	- The track the nest clip lands on still applies its volume and pan over the whole nest clip, so its copy inside starts at full volume and centred. A selection from one track sounds the same nested.
555	- A track [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) isn't copied inside. The one on the nest clip's own track goes on working over the nest clip.
556	
557	The nest clip itself starts at the default position and scale, at full opacity. It has a **Sound** tab only when something inside can make a sound.
558	
559	## Name a nest
560	
561	Nests are named `Nest 1`, `Nest 2` and so on. To give a nest clip your own name, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**), or use the name field at the top of the Clip tab.
562	
563	A double-click on a nest clip opens it, so it doesn't start a rename as it does on other clips.
564	
565	## A nest's size is fixed
566	
567	A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. Changing the [project's size](/projects/canvas-size/) later doesn't re-lay out what's inside, and opening the nest lets you edit its contents but not its size.
568	
569	To change a nest's size:
570	
571	<Steps>
572	
573	1. Press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it.
574	
575	2. Change the project size if you need to.
576	
577	3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd> to nest it again.
578	
579	</Steps>
580	
581	## Un-nest
582	
583	Select one or more nest clips and press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Un-nest**. The item is available when the selection includes a nest clip, and anything else selected is left alone.
584	
585	Every selected nest clip opens back out in one undo step, called Un-nest, or Un-nest Clips for several. What came out is selected.
586	
587	- Clips return at the nest clip's start plus their own times, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's track. Missing tracks are added behind it.
588	- A clip that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) goes on a new front track and isn't lost.
589	- A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents still gives everything back, because trimming a nest hides content and doesn't cut it.
590	- If other clips show the same nest, they keep it. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).
591	
592	:::caution
593	Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume. To change the contents and keep those, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it.
594	:::
595	
596	The settings of the tracks inside the nest don't come out either. Clips that return take on the settings of the timeline tracks they land on.
597	
598	## Nests inside nests
599	
600	A nest can hold other nests, up to eight levels deep. Select a nest clip with other clips and press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or press it while a nest is open.
601	
602	The depth counts the whole project, even while you edit inside a nest, so an edit that looks fine there can still stop at the limit. The same goes for the project's limits of 64 tracks and 4,096 clips, and a nest's own tracks count towards the 64.
603	
604	## When Nest won't work
605	
606	**Clip ▸ Nest** is greyed out with nothing selected, and when the only selected clip is already a nest clip, since wrapping one nest in another on its own changes nothing you can see.
607	
608	With the item available, two things can still stop a nest. Frame Job beeps, changes nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.
609	
610	- **Something unselected is in the way.** The nest clip would overlap a clip you didn't select on its track, by more than the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) allows. This often means an unselected clip sits inside the span. Select it too, or move it.
611	- **The selection holds an adjustment clip.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest.
612	
613	If the nest clip overlaps the clip before it by an amount the rule allows, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
614	
615	## With an agent
616	
617	`nest` can name the nest as it's made, [`set_clip`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_clip) renames a nest clip, and [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/) lists every nest with its own tracks and clips. [`unnest`](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#unnest) opens one nest clip at a time, and gives an error on any other kind of clip. The clips it brings back are new clips, with new ids. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#nest) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
618	
619	## Related
620	
621	- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
622	- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)
623	- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
624	=================== inside-a-nest
625	---
626	title: "Work inside a nest"
627	description: "Open a nest to edit its clips in place, find your way back out, and see what stays project-wide while you're inside."
628	---
629	
630	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
631	
632	Open a [nest](/editing/nests/) to change the clips inside it without taking the group apart. The nest clip keeps its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, which [Un-nest](/editing/nests/#un-nest) would throw away.
633	
634	<AtAGlance
635	  menu={['Clip ▸ Open Nest', 'Clip ▸ Close Nest']}
636	  keys={['⌘↓', '⌘↑']}
637	  where={['Double-click a nest clip', 'The breadcrumb, in the corner above the track headers']}
638	  tools="set_scope"
639	/>
640	
641	## Open a nest
642	
643	Double-click a nest clip. You can also select one nest clip and choose **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>).
644	
645	**Clip ▸ Open Nest** needs exactly one nest clip selected, so it's greyed out with two selected. A double-click works whatever else is selected, because it opens the clip you clicked.
646	
647	A nest can hold nests. Open one the same way from inside, down to eight levels.
648	
649	Because a double-click opens a nest clip, it can't rename one. Use **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) or the name field in the Clip tab.
650	
651	## Come back out
652	
653	Choose **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>), or click the [breadcrumb](#use-the-breadcrumb). Either one goes out one level, and the nest clip you went in through is selected again.
654	
655	**Clip ▸ Close Nest** is greyed out at the top level. **Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are both greyed out while you're typing in a field, so <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> stay with the text.
656	
657	## Use the breadcrumb
658	
659	While a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as `Timeline › Intro`, with a back arrow in front of it.
660	
661	- It shows the last two levels: the one you'd return to, then the one you're in, in bold. Hover over it for the full path.
662	- A level is named after the nest clip you went in through, so renaming that clip changes the path.
663	- A long name is shortened in the middle, so `Lower Third 1` and `Lower Third 2` still look different.
664	
665	Click anywhere in the corner to go out one level, the same as <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. A double-click counts as one click, so to go up two levels, click twice with a pause or press <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> twice.
666	
667	With no nest open, the corner is empty and does nothing.
668	
669	## What you see inside
670	
671	The timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips, with time counted from the start of the nest. That's all of its contents, including anything the nest clip's [trim](/editing/nest-copies/#trim-a-nest-clip) is hiding on the outer timeline.
672	
673	The canvas shows the nest at its fixed size, without the nest clip's position, scale, opacity or fades, and you hear it without the nest clip's volume. You're seeing the group by itself, and the nest clip's settings apply again when you leave.
674	
675	## Where the playhead goes
676	
677	The playhead moves with you, so the frame under it doesn't change. It also carries back out. If a nest clip starts at 10 s and the playhead is at 12 s, you go in at 2 s. Move to 3 s, come out, and you're at 13 s.
678	
679	That holds while the playhead is over the nest clip. If it's before the clip when you double-click, you go in at the nest's first frame and come out at the clip's start. If it's past the clip's end, or you move past that point inside, the playhead is on a part of the nest the clip doesn't play, so the canvas inside shows a frame the outer timeline never will.
680	
681	Going in or out also stops playback.
682	
683	## Going in and out isn't an edit
684	
685	Opening or closing a nest makes no undo step and doesn't mark the project as changed.
686	
687	- **Selection:** going in clears the selection. Coming out selects the nest clip again.
688	- **In/out range:** it's cleared both ways, because a range means one thing inside a nest and another on the timeline. You can set a new [range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside, and looping and Ripple Delete use it as they do on the timeline.
689	- **Reopening:** a project always opens on its timeline, even if you saved with a nest open.
690	
691	## Edit inside a nest
692	
693	Every clip edit works inside a nest, with times counted from the start of the nest. That includes **Clip ▸ Nest**, which makes a nest inside this one, and **Clip ▸ Un-nest**.
694	
695	Each edit is one step on the project's single undo history:
696	
697	- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> after you've come out still undoes an edit you made inside.
698	- If an undo removes the nest you're in, you land in the deepest level that's left, and the in/out range clears.
699	
700	When more than one clip shows this nest, your edit reaches all of them. See [Shared copies](/editing/nest-copies/#shared-copies).
701	
702	The nest clip on the outer timeline keeps its length whatever you do inside. Material you add past its end stays hidden until you drag the clip's end out, and if the contents get shorter, the clip shows nothing over what's left of it.
703	
704	## What stays project-wide
705	
706	Some things belong to the project, not to the nest you have open. They still work, and they change the whole project.
707	
708	- **Media:** the Media tab lists the project's media. Adding, relinking or removing a file works as usual. Drag a row from the Media tab onto the nest's timeline to put its clip in the nest. A file dragged from the Finder onto the timeline opens as a project of its own, so add it on the Media tab first.
709	- **The Document tab:** it shows the project's settings. Changing the project's size doesn't change the nest's size, which is [fixed](/editing/nests/#a-nests-size-is-fixed).
710	- **Markers:** the Document tab's list stays, but the ruler shows none. You can still rename a marker, change its **Chapter** box or delete it. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
711	- **Export:** **File ▸ Export…** writes the whole timeline, not the nest. A range you set inside a nest can't be used, so the **Range** pop-up stays on **Whole project**. Close the nest and set the range on the timeline.
712	
713	**File ▸ Save Frame…** is the exception: it saves what the canvas shows, so with a nest open you get a frame of the nest.
714	
715	## What you can't use inside a nest
716	
717	| Command | While a nest is open |
718	| --- | --- |
719	| **Mark ▸ Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker** | Greyed out, and <kbd>M</kbd> beeps. **Go** in the Document tab's Markers list is greyed out too. A marker's time is on the outer timeline, and the playhead inside a nest counts from the nest's start. |
720	| **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** | Greyed out. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) only works on the timeline, never inside a nest. |
721	| **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject** | Greyed out, and the Picture tab has no **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/). |
722	| **File ▸ New Project from Range…** | Greyed out. See [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/). |
723	| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | Greyed out. See [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/). |
724	| **File ▸ Rename Graphic…** | Greyed out. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/). |
725	| **Track ▸ Mix…** | **Compressor** and **Limit peaks** are greyed out, because a nest's mix plays through the track that holds the nest clip. The track's volume and pan still work. |
726	
727	## Limits count the whole project
728	
729	A project holds up to 4,096 clips and 64 tracks, and nests go eight levels deep. Clips and tracks are counted across the timeline and every nest together, and the depth is counted from the timeline. So an edit that looks fine inside a nest can still take the whole project over. When it would, Frame Job shows an alert naming the limit and changes nothing.
730	
731	A nest's contents count once, however many clips show it. Un-nest the last clip showing a nest to take its tracks out of the count. Deleting that clip instead leaves the nest's clips and tracks counted.
732	
733	## With an agent
734	
735	An agent can open a nest in the window with [`set_scope`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_scope), as you would. This only changes the view, so it adds no undo step, and `set_scope` with no arguments comes back out. Given a nest two clips show, it goes in through the earlier one.
736	
737	An agent can also edit inside any nest without opening it, by naming the nest on the edit. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/), which lists the edits that can't be made that way.
738	
739	## Related
740	
741	- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
742	- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)
743	- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
744	- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
745	- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
746	=================== nest-copies
747	---
748	title: "Shared and independent nest copies"
749	description: "Know which copies of a nest clip edit together, make a copy of your own, and see what trimming a nest clip really does."
750	---
751	
752	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
753	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
754	
755	A nest clip is a view of a [nest](/editing/nests/), not the nest itself. Two clips can show one nest, so an edit inside it reaches both. This page covers which copies share their contents, how to get one that doesn't, and what a trim does to a nest clip.
756	
757	<AtAGlance
758	  menu={['Edit ▸ Duplicate', 'Clip ▸ Split', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest', 'Clip ▸ Nest']}
759	  keys={['⌘D', '⌘T', '⇧⌘G', '⌘G']}
760	  where="⌥-drag a nest clip"
761	  tools={['duplicate', 'split', 'paste', 'unnest', 'nest']}
762	/>
763	
764	## Shared copies
765	
766	These all leave you with clips that show one nest:
767	
768	| Do this | You get |
769	| --- | --- |
770	| **Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>) | A second clip showing the same nest, straight after the selection. |
771	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag a nest clip | A second clip showing the same nest, where you drop it. |
772	| **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>) | Two clips showing the same nest, cut at the playhead. |
773	
774	[Open](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest) any of them and edit, and every clip showing that nest changes.
775	
776	Only the contents are shared. Each nest clip keeps its own place on the timeline, its own length, and its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume.
777	
778	[Un-nesting](/editing/nests/#un-nest) one clip gives you its contents as ordinary clips and leaves the others showing the nest. The nest goes when you un-nest the last clip that shows it.
779	
780	:::caution[A split nest clip starts again]
781	A nest clip always plays from the nest's first frame. So when you split one, the second part starts from the top of the nest, not from where you cut, and the join shows. The same goes for anything else that cuts through a nest clip, such as a ripple delete over a range.
782	
783	To cut the contents at a moment, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and split inside it.
784	:::
785	
786	## Make an independent copy
787	
788	To get a copy you can edit on its own, turn a duplicate back into clips and nest them again.
789	
790	<Steps>
791	
792	1. Select the nest clip and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. The selection stays on the original.
793	
794	2. Click the new copy, then press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it. Its contents come out as ordinary clips, all selected.
795	
796	3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>. Those clips become a new nest of their own.
797	
798	</Steps>
799	
800	Un-nesting drops the copy's own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, so set those again on the new nest clip. The new nest also takes the project's current size, which may differ from the original's. Un-nesting gives back everything in the nest, so a [trim](#trim-a-nest-clip) on the copy is gone too.
801	
802	This separates one level. A nest clip among the contents still shows the same inner nest as the original, so an edit inside that inner nest reaches both. Un-nest it too, before step 3, if you need it separate.
803	
804	:::caution[Copy and Paste don't work on a nest clip]
805	**Edit ▸ Copy** puts the nest clip on the clipboard but not what's inside it. **Edit ▸ Paste** then pastes nothing and shows an alert saying the pasted clip shows a nest "which the payload does not carry". That's true of any selection with a nest clip in it, in this project or another one.
806	
807	**Edit ▸ Cut** still removes the clip, so after a failed paste, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> until it's back.
808	:::
809	
810	## Trim a nest clip
811	
812	Trimming a nest clip changes how much of the nest plays. It never cuts anything out of the nest. The clip always plays from the nest's first frame for as long as the clip lasts, which makes its two edges behave differently from a media clip's:
813	
814	| Drag | What happens |
815	| --- | --- |
816	| The end edge in | The tail of the nest is hidden. |
817	| The end edge out | More of the nest plays. Past the end of the contents, the clip shows nothing. The contents set no limit on how far you can drag. |
818	| The start edge later | The clip starts later and the whole nest moves later with it. The opening still plays, and the tail is what gets hidden. |
819	| The start edge earlier | The nest moves earlier with it, and more of the tail plays. |
820	
821	So you can't hide a nest's opening with a trim. To do that, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it, which changes every clip showing the nest.
822	
823	**Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>) gives back everything, however short the clip was trimmed. Hidden clips come back where they sit in the nest, counted from the nest clip's start, even past the clip's end. One that would then collide with what's after it goes on a new track in front.
824	
825	## With an agent
826	
827	An agent can make the independent copy in one step. `paste` makes a separate nest when it's given the nest's contents as well as the clip, with every level inside it, and editing the copy leaves the original alone. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste).
828	
829	## Related
830	
831	- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
832	- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
833	- [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/)
834	- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
835	- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
836	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
837
